  • A source that opts out of the address check removes the protection for that source. A reviewer must approve each opt-out.
  • Open point: the Tavily daily credit budget.
  • Open point: the retention rule for rejected documents.
  • Open point: the review of the Mistral data-retention terms.
  • Open point: the OCR model pin.

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Local folder strategy - rejected as unsafe. A path from a source or from a user can reach files outside the intended folder. It adds a path-traversal risk for little value.
  • Per-source YAML configuration - rejected. The sources are few, reviewed in code, and typed. YAML brings back the registration layer that ADR-0014 removed, and it moves errors from import time to run time.
  • Class-level singleton registry - rejected. Hidden global state makes tests depend on each other. Module-level instances next to the base classes are simple, and tests can use a private Registry.
  • Inheritance for strategies - rejected. The strategies share no state, so a Protocol is enough.
  • Pin the connection to the checked address - not done now. It closes the DNS rebinding window, but it adds transport code that the project must maintain.

docs.title: ADR-0017: SeaweedFS as the S3 object store
Context
docs.text:
The document fetcher (ADR-0016) has a MinIO strategy. It reads documents from an S3 bucket through the Python minio SDK. The first-start init also needs an S3 store. The compose stack has no S3 service yet. The first plan was to run the MinIO community image.

MinIO community edition is no longer a safe base:

  • MinIO stopped publishing community images on Docker Hub and Quay in October 2025.
  • The upstream repository shows "no longer maintained" and is read-only. The repository banner gives 2026-04-25 as the archive date. One aggregator says February 2026. This conflict is not resolved.
  • The last upstream release is RELEASE.2025-10-15.
  • A tutorial dated 2026-01-28 confirms that the images do not get updates. It says that the old Quay examples still run.
  • On 2026-11-05, an anonymous pull of minio/minio from Docker Hub failed (repository missing or needs authorization). Quay returned 401.

The stack must fit in 4-6 GB RAM. The data is a few GB of legal PDFs on a single node.

docs.title: Spike
docs.text:
The maintainer ran one spike on 2026-11-05 on the dev host (Docker 28.5.1). Each candidate got the same test:

  • Six minio SDK calls: bucket_exists, make_bucket, put_object, stat_object, get_object, list_objects.
  • A hardened container: read-only root, cap_drop: ALL, and no-new-privileges.
  • Idle RAM from docker stats.
  • A crash test: write 200 objects of 4 KiB and one 20 MB multipart object, send docker kill -s KILL, restart, and verify all bytes.

Four candidates passed all tests.

Candidate License Idle RAM User Notes SeaweedFS 4.52 (chrislusf/seaweedfs:4.52) Apache-2.0 38 MiB UID 1000 Image is 780 MB. Entrypoint override needed. Telemetry on by default. Silo (pgsty/minio fork) AGPL 69 MiB root, caps dropped Docker Hub image lags the GitHub release. One company controls the fork. Chainguard MinIO (cgr.dev/chainguard/minio) not checked 60 MiB UID 65532 Free tier shows only latest. Terms not verified. Garage 2.5.0 AGPL 7 MiB root, caps dropped Single node is not an intended use case.

SeaweedFS details from the spike:

  • The seaweed user owns /data in the image, so a fresh named volume works.
  • The default entrypoint fails when all capabilities are dropped (su-exec: setgroups). Compose must set the entrypoint to /usr/bin/weed.
  • SeaweedFS sends anonymous statistics to telemetry.seaweedfs.com by default. The flag -master.telemetry=false turns this off.
  • The S3 keys come from a JSON file (-s3.config). The bucket comes from -bucket.
  • The spike did not test a healthcheck.

docs.title: Engineer opinion
docs.text: This evidence is weak. It comes from Hacker News threads (about spring and September 2026) and from blogs. SeaweedFS had the most positive single-node reports. One blog (2026-07-30) reports 30-50 MB idle RAM. Engineers also warn about sparse docs, and one report describes a failure under concurrent writes. The maintainer could not reach or find Reddit, lobste.rs, or conference talks on this topic.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. SeaweedFS in weed mini mode is the S3 object store. It serves the fetch MinIO strategy and the first-start init. The license is Apache-2.0.
  2. The client stays. The Python minio SDK stays as the client. It uses the S3 API, so the strategy code does not change.
  3. Only the compose service changes. weed mini runs master, volume, filer, and S3 in one process, so the stack has one container for the store.

docs.title: Not verified
docs.text:
The spike does not prove these points. Treat them as open risks.

  • Power-loss durability for every candidate. kill -9 keeps the OS page cache, so the crash test does not simulate a power loss.
  • Behaviour under concurrent writes.
  • A vulnerability scan of the image.
  • The SeaweedFS healthcheck command.
  • How Dependabot handles an image pinned by tag and digest.
  • How SeaweedFS ages with several GB of data.
  • The effect of the 780 MB SeaweedFS image on small hosts.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Pin the image by tag and by digest.
  • Override the entrypoint to /usr/bin/weed. The override removes the switch to UID 1000 that the image entrypoint does. Set user: "1000:1000" in the compose service. Root with cap_drop: ALL cannot write the fresh /data volume, which the seaweed user owns, and weed mini stops at its writable-directory check.
  • Turn telemetry off with -master.telemetry=false.
  • Supply the S3 keys from a mounted file or from env that the init renders. The infra change makes this choice, not this ADR.
  • Add a restore test and a backup note to the infra change.
  • The MinIO class and the MINIO_* settings keep their names for now. A rename is a separate decision.
  • The store is a single process on a single node. It has no replication.
  • Revisit this decision if SeaweedFS fails a power-loss test or a CVE scan. Silo is the first fallback. Chainguard MinIO is the second fallback.

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Silo (pgsty/minio fork) - fallback 1. It passed the spike with 69 MiB idle RAM, and a curl health check returned 200. It runs as root with all capabilities dropped. The newest Docker Hub tag is from 2026-08-04, but GitHub shows a release from 2026-10-26, so the Hub image lags. One company controls the fork. The license is AGPL.
  • Chainguard MinIO (cgr.dev/chainguard/minio) - fallback 2. It passed the spike with 60 MiB idle RAM and runs as UID 65532. Its version string RELEASE.2026-10-23 differs from the last upstream release. Chainguard probably patches the archived source, but this is an inference and is not verified. The free tier shows only the latest tag. The maintainer did not verify the terms from an official page.
  • Garage 2.5.0 - rejected. It passed the spike with 7 MiB idle RAM. It runs as root with all capabilities dropped. It needs s3_region = us-east-1, or the SDK fails with AuthorizationHeaderMalformed. The Garage docs and a blog post (2026-04-18) say that a single node (replication factor 1) is not an intended use case. The default LMDB metadata database can corrupt after an unclean shutdown, and fsync is off by default. The license is AGPL.
  • RustFS - rejected. It has several CVEs from 2026, one rated 9.8. Users report data loss with a single replica. Its maturity claims conflict.
  • Ceph RGW - rejected. It needs about 4 GiB of RAM per OSD, so it does not fit the 4-6 GB budget.
  • Keep MinIO, built from source - rejected. The project must build and maintain the image, and the upstream is archived, so no security fixes arrive.

docs.title: ADR-0018: Valkey as the Celery broker and result store
Context
docs.text:
The stack uses Redis only as the Celery broker and result store (ADR-0006). No data is kept on disk. The compose service runs redis:8.8.4-alpine.

The goal is to avoid license risk now and in the future. Redis 8 is offered under a choice of three licenses: RSALv2, SSPLv1, or AGPLv3 (source: the Redis licensing page, https://redis.io/legal/licenses/). RSALv2 and SSPLv1 are source-available licenses and are not approved by the OSI. AGPLv3 is an open source license with network copyleft.

The project does not change Redis and runs it as a separate service, so this ADR does not claim a proven conflict with the MIT license today. The risk is for the future. A self-hosting operator who changes or offers Redis as a service can fall under these terms, and the project cannot give a clear answer. This is not legal advice. Redis has changed its license once already, and the vendor can change it again. Valkey is the BSD-3-Clause fork of Redis 7.2. It is an open community project under LF Projects, LLC, not a single-vendor product. It speaks the same protocol.

Sources, read on 2026-11-06 (page summaries, not the full license texts):

  • Redis licensing page, https://redis.io/legal/licenses/: Redis 8.0.0 and later is offered under RSALv2, SSPLv1, or AGPLv3. Redis 7.2 and earlier stay under BSD-3-Clause.
  • Redis security policy, https://github.com/redis/redis/security/policy: 7.2.x is listed as supported, with support extended until the end of support of 7.4.
  • Valkey repository, https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey: license BSD-3-Clause, hosted as an open community project under LF Projects, LLC. The LICENSE file was not read.

docs.title: Spike
docs.text:
The maintainer ran one spike on 2026-11-06 on the dev host (Docker 28.5.1).

  • Image: valkey/valkey:8-alpine (Valkey 8.1.11, amd64, 42 MB).
  • Container: same hardening as the redis service. It has a read-only root, cap_drop: ALL, no-new-privileges, user 999:999, a tmpfs /data, 32 MB RAM, 0.5 CPU, and 100 PIDs.
  • Command: valkey-server --requirepass "$REDIS_PASSWORD" --save "" --appendonly no.
  • Client: Celery 5.6.3 and redis 6.4.0 from the project venv, with a worker on the host (-P solo).

Results:

Check Result Container starts with the hardening above Pass redis-cli ping and valkey-cli ping with REDISCLI_AUTH PONG (both CLIs ship) valkey-cli ping without a password NOAUTH Authentication required redis Python client without a password AuthenticationError celery inspect ping pong, 1 node online Task add(2, 3) through broker and result backend Result 5 Memory after the test 4.1 MiB of 32 MiB

The spike did not save the Valkey server log. The checks above come from command output only.

docs.title: Full-stack check
docs.text:
On 2026-11-06 the maintainer ran the compose stack with the Valkey image under a separate project name, with a throwaway env file:

  • postgres, redis, s3, app, and celery-worker all reached the healthy state. The init service exited with code 0.
  • celery -A tasks.celery_app inspect ping in the worker returned pong, one node online.
  • A client on the backend network without a password got NOAUTH Authentication required.
  • The Docker test suite (docker compose --profile test ... run --rm test) gave 946 passed and 18 skipped. The skips were 13 PostgreSQL integration tests ("PostgreSQL unavailable" with the example env file) and 4 live Sejm tests. The maintainer did not look for a test of the broker path in the suite, so the Celery pong above is the only recorded broker check on the compose stack.

The image has no default user (it runs as root), so compose must set user: "999:999". The spike did this and Valkey started with the tmpfs /data.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Valkey replaces Redis 8 as the broker and result store. The license is BSD-3-Clause.
  2. The clients stay. Celery and the Python redis client do not change. The env names REDIS_PASSWORD and the redis:// URLs keep their names.
  3. Only the compose service changes. Pin the image by tag and by digest.

docs.title: Not verified
docs.text:
• A full run of the project stack and the compose tests on Valkey.
  • Behaviour under load, and long-running tasks with retries.
  • The image architectures other than amd64.
  • Whether the image is a Docker Official Image or a publisher image.
  • A vulnerability scan of the image.
  • How Dependabot handles an image pinned by tag and digest.
  • Celery does not list Valkey as a supported broker. The spike shows that it works. A future Valkey change could break it.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Change the redis service in docker/docker-compose.yml: image, command (valkey-server), and healthcheck (valkey-cli ping).
  • Set user: "999:999" explicitly.
  • Update docs/operations.md, docker/README.md, and the compose tests.
  • Keep the service name redis for now. A rename is a separate decision.
  • Plan the cutover. The broker keeps no data on disk, so a restart or the switch from Redis to Valkey discards queued tasks and stored results. Before the switch, pause producers, drain pending and active tasks, and save any result that is still needed.
  • Revisit this decision if a Celery release breaks on Valkey, or if Redis returns to a permissive license.

docs.title: Alternatives Considered
docs.text:
• Keep Redis 8 - rejected. The license is RSALv2, SSPLv1, or AGPLv3.
  • Redis 7.2.x - rejected. Redis lists the 7.2.x series as BSD-3-Clause and as supported for security fixes, so it is valid today. It does not remove the license risk. It is the last BSD line from Redis, it gets no new features, and the vendor controls the license of every later version. The project would have to leave Redis later anyway. Valkey removes the risk now. Support for 7.2.x is extended until the end of support of 7.4 (security policy, read on 2026-11-06).
  • Postgres-based queue - rejected. Celery has no stable Postgres broker, and it adds load on the database.
  • KeyDB, Dragonfly - not tested. Not needed, because Valkey passed.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • ADR-0006 (Celery and Redis)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: No admin UI creates or deactivates users. Only the seed script creates users. The DB trigger trg_users_session_version bumps session_version when is_active changes. The principal has email and role only, with no user id and no tenant. The users RLS policy is tenant-only: with no tenant set, a list returns no rows and an insert fails the WITH CHECK. See requirements.md.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Path 1: store-centric. Rules inside PostgreSQLStore. Smallest diff. Testable only through the store.
  • Path 2: hexagonal service layer. core/users service and a UserRepository port. The store is the adapter.
  • Path 3: database-centric. SQL functions and triggers enforce the rules. The mutation gate does not measure plpgsql.
  • Path 4: async Celery workflow. Effort L. The hash crosses Redis. The 1 second target is at risk.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Path 2, chosen by the owner at the design gate. The architect and DBA reviewed it and approved it with the changes below. - src/core/users/ holds service.py, ports.py and errors.py. It imports only core.security and its own port. It imports no plugins.* and no streamlit. The page wires PostgreSQLStore into the service. - Errors: UserCreateRefusedError, UserNotFoundError, SelfDeactivationError, LastAdminError, plus PrincipalRequiredError from core. - Every service call: raise PrincipalRequiredError if get_current_tenant() is empty. Then call require_admin_principal(). Then load the actor row by normalised principal email under the tenant. It must be an active admin, or the call raises PrincipalRequiredError. This binds the principal to the tenant and gives the actor id for the audit event. - The tenant comes from get_current_tenant(), which login sets (auth.py). It is never an argument or a form field. - create_user(email, password, role, name) returns {id, tenant_id, email, role, name, is_active}. Validation: password 12 or more characters and 72 or fewer UTF-8 bytes (move the init_stack constants to core.security.passwords), email with one @ and at most 256 characters, name at most 256, role by valid_role. Every failure raises UserCreateRefusedError. hash_password always runs before the insert. There is no existence pre-check. The adapter maps only SQLSTATE 23505 on uq_users_email to UserCreateRefusedError. Any other DB error stays a generic DB error. Roll back on every error. - list_users() reuses the existing store method and adds a tenant_id predicate on top of RLS. It orders by email. It returns records without the hash. - deactivate_user(user_id): read the target under RLS. A missing or foreign id raises UserNotFoundError. Self is detected by comparing the target id with the actor row id, and it raises SelfDeactivationError. If the target is an admin, lock the tenant's active admin rows with FOR UPDATE ORDER BY id first, with no LIMIT and no SKIP LOCKED, and nothing else locked before. If the actor is not in the locked set, raise PrincipalRequiredError. If the locked set holds the target and has one row or fewer, raise LastAdminError (defence in depth: with a verified actor distinct from the target, the set always has two rows or more). An already inactive admin target is not in the locked set, so the call returns False. If the target has role user, lock the actor row FOR SHARE (role admin, active, same tenant), then lock the target FOR UPDATE. No row for the actor raises PrincipalRequiredError. Then UPDATE users SET is_active = false WHERE id = :id AND is_active RETURNING id. Zero rows means an idempotent no-op. Self is checked before last admin. The existing trigger bumps session_version. - The page lives in src/ui/pages/users.py. app.py registers it in the same is_admin block as the fetch page. The page calls require_admin() first and maps errors to fixed messages. - PostgreSQLStore.create_user keeps its signature. The seed script still uses it. - require_admin, require_admin_principal and check_privilege_escalation stay unchanged.

docs.title: Port signatures
docs.text:
The UserRepository Protocol in src/core/users/ports.py has four methods. PostgreSQLStore implements all four with the same parameter names, kinds and defaults (T5 checks this).

Record type, in ports.py: 

class UserRecord(TypedDict):
    id: str
    tenant_id: str
    email: str
    role: str
    name: str
    is_active: bool
UserRecord never holds password_hash or session_version. plugins/relational_db/mappers.py adds user_to_record(row: User) -> UserRecord. The existing user_to_dict stays unchanged for create_user and get_user_by_email.

Methods: 

def find_active_admin(self, email: str) -> UserRecord | None: ...
def insert_user(
    self, *, email: str, password_hash: str, role: str, name: str, actor_id: str
) -> UserRecord: ...
def list_users(self) -> list[UserRecord]: ...
def deactivate_user(self, user_id: str, *, actor_id: str) -> bool: ...

Rules for each method in the store: - Every method reads the tenant from get_current_tenant(). Every query adds a tenant_id predicate on top of RLS. - find_active_admin(email): the service passes the email from normalise_email(principal.email). The store compares it exactly. It returns the row only if role = 'admin' and is_active are true. Otherwise it returns None. With no tenant set, it returns None and runs no SQL. It raises no domain error. The service maps None to PrincipalRequiredError. - insert_user(...): the service passes a normalised email and a bcrypt hash. The store sets a new uuid4 id, the current tenant and is_active = true. The store locks the actor row FOR SHARE (role admin, active, same tenant) in the same transaction, before the insert. It returns the new record. Errors, in check order: PrincipalRequiredError with no tenant set, before any SQL. PrincipalRequiredError when the actor is not an active admin of the tenant (nothing is inserted). UserCreateRefusedError only for SQLSTATE 23505 on uq_users_email. Every other DB error is re-raised unmapped. The transaction rolls back on every error. - list_users(): it keeps the existing name and has no parameters. Its return annotation changes from list[dict[str, Any]] to list[UserRecord]. It orders by email. With no tenant set, it returns [] and raises no error. DB errors propagate unmapped. - deactivate_user(user_id, *, actor_id): the service passes the id of the row that find_active_admin returned. The store does the self check inside the lock transaction, so the check and the update see the same state. It returns True when the update changed one row, and False for an idempotent no-op on an inactive target. Errors, in check order: PrincipalRequiredError with no tenant set, before any SQL. UserNotFoundError for a missing or foreign id. SelfDeactivationError when user_id == actor_id. PrincipalRequiredError when the actor is not an active admin of the tenant. LastAdminError when the locked admin set has one row or fewer. The transaction rolls back on every error. - The store imports the domain errors from core.users.errors and PrincipalRequiredError from core.security. The core.users package still imports no plugins.*. - The service audit event holds actor id, target id, action and the changed flag from deactivate_user.

  • Actor check in the write transaction: find_active_admin stays a fast pre-check in the service (the principal holds an email, not a user id). The store re-checks the actor row under the same transaction and is the authority. The lock order is one rule: admin rows in id order first, then the non-admin target. Never take the actor FOR SHARE before the ordered admin lock, because two crossed deactivations would deadlock. The target role is read without a lock, which is safe while no API changes a role. A future role update must lock admin rows first.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• No migration and no new dependency. No new index: ix_users_tenant_id and uq_users_email serve the queries.
  • Unit tests use a fake port. Integration tests use real Postgres, including a two-session test for the last-admin lock and leak tests with no tenant set at store level.
  • A conformance test keeps the port and the store in step.
  • A deactivated user's cookie fails both the is_active check and the session_version check on the next request.
  • Accepted risk: the generic duplicate message still tells an admin that the email exists somewhere, because email is unique across tenants and login needs that. The probe is now rate-limited per acting admin (default 10 creates per 3600 s, USER_CREATE_MAX and USER_CREATE_WINDOW_SECONDS, counted in Redis). When Redis is down, creation is refused (fail closed). Per-tenant email uniqueness stays an open owner decision: it needs a login change and is not part of this change.
  • A future reactivate or demote must take the same admin lock set.
  • Follow-ups, need owner approval: a trg_users_last_admin DB backstop, a DB audit table, and a fix of the stale setting = '' wording about users in the project CLAUDE.md. The wording is wrong for users since migration b7e2d41c9a30.

docs.title: Requirements: admin-user-management
docs.text: An admin-only Streamlit page to create and deactivate users. Follow-up left out of scope by the login UI task.

docs.title: Business Goals
docs.text:
• A tenant admin adds and removes users from the UI. Today only the seed script creates users.
  • Scope is create, list and deactivate. Reactivate, password reset and role change are out of scope.
  • A new user joins the admin's own tenant. The tenant comes from the tenant context that login sets, never from the form.
  • Test: an admin creates a user who then logs in. An admin deactivates that user and the user cannot log in again.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• ADR-0013: streamlit-authenticator, bcrypt through hash_password, RBAC admin and user. ADR-0003: tenant isolation by tenant_id and RLS.
  • Facts in the code: users.email is unique across tenants and the DB checks email = lower(btrim(email)). The trigger trg_users_session_version bumps session_version when is_active or password_hash changes. PostgreSQLStore has no deactivate_user. create_user does not validate the role and does not handle a duplicate email.
  • The admin can create both roles. The server validates the role with valid_role. The form never sets the tenant.
  • The admin types the initial password. The server enforces 12 or more characters and at most 72 UTF-8 bytes (the init_stack limits), hashes it, and never logs or shows it. Email is at most 256 characters, name is at most 256.
  • The server refuses self-deactivation and deactivation of the last active admin of the tenant.
  • No change weakens require_admin, require_admin_principal or check_privilege_escalation. The page calls require_admin() first, and the service re-checks the principal on the server side.
  • Tenant guard rules apply: the tenant comes from get_current_tenant(), never an argument. An empty tenant raises an error before any SQL. A foreign row behaves as a missing row.
  • Python 3.13, Streamlit, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL. No new dependency.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• A duplicate email, in the own tenant or another tenant, shows one generic message: "Cannot create this user." The message still reveals that the email exists somewhere (email is unique across tenants). The probe is rate-limited per acting admin: see decision.md.
  • Email input is trimmed and lowercased before the write. A blank or malformed email is refused.
  • A role outside VALID_ROLES is refused on the server.
  • Deactivating an already inactive user is idempotent: no error and no extra session_version bump.
  • Deactivating an id from another tenant or an unknown id behaves as a missing row.
  • Two admins deactivate the last two admins at the same time: the last-admin check must hold under concurrency.
  • A user with role user opens the page URL directly: the page stops with "Admin role required." and no data loads.
  • A demoted or deactivated admin loses the page on the next request.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Each action is one transaction. On a DB error the page shows a generic error and no stack trace.
  • A DB error can mean the commit outcome is unknown: PostgreSQL may commit and the connection may fail before the client sees the reply. The page message says so: "Database error. The action may have succeeded. Check the user list before you try again." The admin checks the user table before a retry. After a commit, a retried create gets the generic duplicate message and a retried deactivate is an idempotent no-op. After a rollback, the retry does the action. Either way a retry does not create a second user.
  • The log never holds a password or a hash.
  • Audit is a structured log event (stdlib logging, extra fields; structlog is not a dependency yet) with actor id, target id and action. A DB audit table is a follow-up, not in scope.
  • If the redis or login lookup is down, the existing login behaviour stays unchanged.
  • The admin sees a clear error for invalid input. The admin never sees a stack trace.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
• Integration test: the old cookie of a deactivated user fails on the next request because session_version differs.
  • Leak tests: 0 cross-tenant rows read or written by the new store methods.
  • Role user: 0 successful calls to create or deactivate, at page level and at service level.
  • Tests cover create, deactivate, duplicate email and privilege escalation, as unit and integration tests.
  • New code meets the repo coverage and mutation gates (CONTRIBUTING.md).
  • Page action on local Postgres returns in under 1 second.

docs.title: Path 1: store-centric monolith
docs.text: Rules live in PostgreSQLStore. create_user is hardened and deactivate_user is new. Both call require_admin_principal() first. The tenant comes from get_current_tenant(), never from an argument. The page is a thin form. - Deactivate: one transaction, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the tenant rows in id order, then the checks (missing or foreign, already inactive, self, last admin), then UPDATE. The existing trigger bumps session_version. - Files: postgres.py, one page, error classes. About 3 files plus tests. - Effort: S to M. - Risks: the principal has only email and role, so self-detection compares emails. Dropping tenant_id from create_user breaks the seed script and tests. Rules are testable only through the store.

docs.title: Path 2: hexagonal service layer
docs.text: New src/core/users/ with service.py, ports.py (UserRepository) and errors.py. The service owns the admin check, validation, hashing, error mapping and audit. PostgreSQLStore implements the port. The page maps form fields to service calls and errors to messages. - Deactivate: the service refuses self by email. The store takes FOR UPDATE on active admin rows, recounts, then updates. An inactive target returns early. - Tests: a fake port gives cheap unit tests and a zero-call assertion for role user. Real Postgres covers integration. - Effort: M. - Risks: self-match by email. The lock needs a two-session test. The port and the store can drift, so a conformance test is needed. create_user cannot be reused as is.

docs.title: Path 3: database-centric enforcement
docs.text: A new Alembic migration adds SQL functions admin_create_user and admin_deactivate_user, a ck_users_role_valid check and a trg_users_last_admin backstop trigger. PostgreSQL enforces tenant, role, last admin and self-deactivation. Python hashes the password, calls the function and maps errors. A thin service adds require_admin_principal and the audit log. - Effort: M. - Gain: the invariants hold for every caller, including the seed script and a future buggy service. - Risks: the drift test and the RLS hardening checks (owners, grants) must grow. Rules split across SQL and Python can drift. The mutation and coverage gates do not measure plpgsql. Hard to debug. Downgrade is complex.

docs.title: Path 4: async command workflow
docs.text: The page enqueues create_user and deactivate_user as Celery tasks. The worker rebuilds the principal, resolves the tenant from the DB, runs one transaction and writes the outcome to a tenant-scoped status row. The page polls. The bcrypt hash, not the plaintext, travels through Redis. - Effort: L. It adds a task layer, a status table with a migration and a polling UI. failed_tasks.py is listed in the README but missing, so ADR-0006 persistence may need building. - Risks: the hash sits in the broker and in failure records. Latency and a cold worker conflict with the 1 second target. A forged message needs a DB re-check of the actor on every run.

docs.title: QA cases: admin-user-management
docs.text: Tenant A has admins admin1@a.example and admin2@a.example, and user bob@a.example. Tenant B has admin admin@b.example and user eve@b.example.

docs.title: QA-001 Admin creates a user who then logs in
docs.text:
• Covers: Business Goals test, T6
  • Type: functional
  • Given admin1@a.example is logged in to tenant A
  • When admin1 creates carol@a.example, role user, name "Carol Nowak", password "correct-horse-12"
  • Then carol@a.example logs in with that password and lands in tenant A

docs.title: QA-002 Admin deactivates a user who then cannot log in
docs.text:
• Covers: Business Goals test, T3, T6
  • Type: functional
  • Given bob@a.example is active and can log in
  • When admin1 deactivates bob@a.example
  • Then a new login by bob@a.example with the correct password is refused

docs.title: QA-003 Old cookie of a deactivated user fails
docs.text:
• Covers: Success Metric 1, T3
  • Type: security
  • Given bob@a.example holds a valid session cookie
  • When admin1 deactivates bob and bob sends the old cookie on the next request
  • Then the request is refused because the session version differs from the stored one

docs.title: QA-004 New user joins the admin's tenant, not a form tenant
docs.text:
• Covers: Business Goals (tenant from context), T4
  • Type: security
  • Given admin1@a.example is logged in to tenant A and the form has no tenant field
  • When admin1 creates dave@a.example
  • Then the user list of tenant A shows dave@a.example and the list of tenant B does not

docs.title: QA-005 List shows own tenant users only, ordered by email
docs.text:
• Covers: Success Metric 2, T2
  • Type: functional
  • Given tenant A has admin1, admin2, bob and tenant B has admin@b.example and eve@b.example
  • When admin1 opens the users page
  • Then the page shows admin1@a.example, admin2@a.example, bob@a.example in that order and 0 tenant B rows

docs.title: QA-006 List never shows hash or session version
docs.text:
• Covers: Failure Mode (never show password), T2
  • Type: security
  • Given tenant A has 3 users
  • When admin1 views the list
  • Then no row shows a password, a hash or a session version

docs.title: QA-007 Duplicate email in own tenant
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 1, T2, T7
  • Type: edge
  • Given bob@a.example exists in tenant A
  • When admin1 creates bob@a.example with password "correct-horse-12"
  • Then the page shows "Cannot create this user." and the list still holds one bob@a.example

docs.title: QA-008 Duplicate email in another tenant
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 1, T2, T7
  • Type: edge
  • Given eve@b.example exists in tenant B
  • When admin1 creates eve@b.example
  • Then the page shows exactly "Cannot create this user." and the text is identical to the own tenant duplicate

docs.title: QA-009 Duplicate email differs only by case and spaces
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 2, T4
  • Type: edge
  • Given bob@a.example exists
  • When admin1 submits " BOB@A.Example " as the email
  • Then the page shows "Cannot create this user." and no second row exists

docs.title: QA-010 Email is trimmed and lowercased
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 2, T4
  • Type: functional
  • Given no user frank@a.example exists
  • When admin1 creates a user with email " Frank@A.Example "
  • Then the list shows frank@a.example

docs.title: QA-011 Blank email refused
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 2, T4
  • Type: failure
  • Given admin1 is logged in
  • When admin1 submits an email of 3 spaces
  • Then the page shows a clear input error and no user is created

docs.title: QA-012 Malformed email refused
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 2, T4
  • Type: failure
  • Given admin1 is logged in
  • When admin1 submits "no-at-sign.example" and then "a@@b.example"
  • Then both attempts show an input error and create 0 users

docs.title: QA-013 Email length limit
docs.text:
• Covers: Technical Constraints (email max 256), T4
  • Type: edge
  • Given admin1 is logged in
  • When admin1 submits an email of 257 characters, then one of exactly 256 characters
  • Then the 257 character email is refused and the 256 character email is created

docs.title: QA-014 Name length limit
docs.text:
• Covers: Technical Constraints (name max 256), T4
  • Type: edge
  • Given admin1 is logged in
  • When admin1 submits a name of 257 characters, then one of 256 characters
  • Then the 257 character name is refused and the 256 character name is created

docs.title: QA-015 Password shorter than 12 characters
docs.text:
• Covers: Technical Constraints (password), T4
  • Type: failure
  • Given admin1 is logged in
  • When admin1 creates a user with password "short-pw-11" (11 characters)
  • Then the page shows an input error and no user is created

docs.title: QA-016 Password of exactly 12 characters
docs.text:
• Covers: Technical Constraints (password), T4
  • Type: edge
  • Given admin1 is logged in
  • When admin1 creates grace@a.example with password "abcdefghijkl"
  • Then the user is created and logs in with that password

docs.title: QA-017 Password of 72 bytes and 73 bytes
docs.text:
• Covers: Technical Constraints (72 UTF-8 bytes), T4
  • Type: edge
  • Given admin1 is logged in
  • When admin1 submits a 72 byte ASCII password, then a 73 byte ASCII password
  • Then the 72 byte password is accepted and the 73 byte password is refused

docs.title: QA-018 Multibyte password over 72 bytes
docs.text:
• Covers: Technical Constraints (UTF-8 bytes), T4
  • Type: edge
  • Given admin1 is logged in
  • When admin1 submits a password of 37 characters "ł" (74 bytes)
  • Then the password is refused although it has fewer than 72 characters

docs.title: QA-019 Role outside the valid set refused
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 3, T4
  • Type: failure
  • Given admin1 is logged in
  • When a create call arrives with role "superadmin"
  • Then it is refused and no user is created

docs.title: QA-020 Admin creates an admin
docs.text:
• Covers: Technical Constraints (both roles), T4
  • Type: functional
  • Given admin1 is logged in
  • When admin1 creates henry@a.example with role admin
  • Then henry logs in and sees the users page

docs.title: QA-021 Deactivate is idempotent
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 4, T3
  • Type: edge
  • Given bob@a.example is inactive and has session version 5
  • When admin1 deactivates bob again
  • Then no error shows and bob's session version stays 5

docs.title: QA-022 Deactivate an id from another tenant
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 5, T3
  • Type: security
  • Given eve@b.example has a known id in tenant B
  • When admin1 deactivates that id
  • Then the result equals the result for a missing row and eve stays active

docs.title: QA-023 Deactivate an unknown id
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 5, T3
  • Type: failure
  • Given no user has id 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
  • When admin1 deactivates that id
  • Then the page shows a not found message and no row changes

docs.title: QA-024 Self-deactivation refused
docs.text:
• Covers: Technical Constraints (self), T3
  • Type: failure
  • Given admin1 and admin2 are active admins
  • When admin1 deactivates admin1
  • Then the call is refused and admin1 stays active

docs.title: QA-025 Last active admin cannot be deactivated
docs.text:
• Covers: Technical Constraints (last admin), T3
  • Type: failure
  • Given tenant A has exactly 2 active admins, admin1 and admin2, in two separate DB sessions
  • When admin1 deactivates admin2 and admin2 deactivates admin1 at the same time
  • Then exactly one call succeeds, the other raises LastAdminError, and exactly 1 admin stays active
  • Note: a single admin that deactivates itself gets SelfDeactivationError, because self is checked first. LastAdminError is reachable by the race above, or by a store-level call whose actor id is not an admin of the tenant.

docs.title: QA-026 Deactivating one of two admins succeeds
docs.text:
• Covers: Technical Constraints (last admin), T3
  • Type: functional
  • Given tenant A has exactly 2 active admins, admin1 and admin2
  • When admin1 deactivates admin2
  • Then admin2 is inactive and admin1 remains the single active admin

docs.title: QA-027 Self check comes before last-admin check
docs.text:
• Covers: Decision (self before last admin), T3
  • Type: edge
  • Given admin1 is the only active admin of tenant A
  • When admin1 deactivates admin1
  • Then the refusal is the self-deactivation error, not the last admin error

docs.title: QA-028 Concurrent deactivation of the last two admins
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 6, T3
  • Type: edge
  • Given tenant A has exactly 2 active admins, admin1 and admin2, in two sessions
  • When admin1 deactivates admin2 and admin2 deactivates admin1 at the same time
  • Then exactly 1 admin stays active and no deadlock error reaches the admin

docs.title: QA-029 Role user opens the page URL directly
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 7, T7
  • Type: security
  • Given bob@a.example (role user) is logged in
  • When bob opens the users page URL
  • Then the page shows "Admin role required." and loads 0 user rows

docs.title: QA-030 Role user calls create at service level
docs.text:
• Covers: Success Metric 3, T4, T6
  • Type: security
  • Given bob@a.example (role user) is the current principal in tenant A
  • When bob calls create for zed@a.example
  • Then the call is refused and 0 users are created

docs.title: QA-031 Role user calls deactivate at service level
docs.text:
• Covers: Success Metric 3, T4, T6
  • Type: security
  • Given bob is the current principal and admin2 is active
  • When bob calls deactivate for admin2
  • Then the call is refused and admin2 stays active

docs.title: QA-032 Demoted or deactivated admin loses the page
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 8, T7
  • Type: security
  • Given admin2 is logged in and admin1 then deactivates admin2
  • When admin2 sends the next request to the users page
  • Then admin2 gets no page and no data

docs.title: QA-033 Admin principal not found in tenant refused
docs.text:
• Covers: Decision (actor row check), T4
  • Type: security
  • Given a principal with admin role and email ghost@a.example that has no row in tenant A
  • When it calls create
  • Then the call is refused and 0 users are created

docs.title: QA-034 Admin of tenant B cannot act on tenant A
docs.text:
• Covers: Success Metric 2, T2, T3
  • Type: security
  • Given admin@b.example is logged in to tenant B
  • When admin@b.example deactivates the id of bob@a.example
  • Then the result is not found and bob stays active

docs.title: QA-035 No tenant set at service level
docs.text:
• Covers: Technical Constraints (empty tenant), T4
  • Type: security
  • Given an admin principal with no tenant set
  • When it calls create, list and deactivate
  • Then each call is refused and no SQL changes any row

docs.title: QA-036 Leak test with no tenant at store level
docs.text:
• Covers: Success Metric 2, T2, T3
  • Type: security
  • Given tenants A and B hold 5 users in total and no tenant is set
  • When list, insert and deactivate run at store level
  • Then list returns 0 rows, insert raises an error and deactivate changes 0 rows

docs.title: QA-037 Leak test with tenant set
docs.text:
• Covers: Success Metric 2, T2
  • Type: security
  • Given tenant A is set and tenant B holds 2 users
  • When list runs and insert runs
  • Then 0 tenant B rows are read and the new row has tenant A

docs.title: QA-038 DB error on create is generic and the outcome may be unknown
docs.text:
• Covers: Failure Mode 1, T7
  • Type: failure
  • Given the database raises a connection error during create
  • When admin1 creates ivan@a.example
  • Then the page shows a generic error without a stack trace. When the rollback is confirmed, ivan does not exist
  • And the message says the action may have succeeded and tells the admin to check the user list. If the commit happened (the connection failed after the commit), a retry gives the duplicate message, not a second user. If the rollback happened, a retry creates ivan

docs.title: QA-039 DB error on deactivate is generic and the outcome may be unknown
docs.text:
• Covers: Failure Mode 1, T3
  • Type: failure
  • Given the database fails during deactivation of bob
  • When admin1 deactivates bob
  • Then the page shows a generic error, says the action may have succeeded and tells the admin to check the user list. When the rollback is confirmed, bob stays active. If the commit happened, a retry is an idempotent no-op. If the rollback happened, a retry deactivates bob

docs.title: QA-040 Non-duplicate integrity error is not shown as duplicate
docs.text:
• Covers: Failure Mode 1, T2
  • Type: failure
  • Given a database constraint other than the unique email fails on create
  • When admin1 creates judy@a.example
  • Then the page shows the generic error, not "Cannot create this user."

docs.title: QA-041 Logs hold no password or hash
docs.text:
• Covers: Failure Mode 2, T4
  • Type: security
  • Given logs are captured and admin1 creates kim@a.example with password "Sup3r-secret-pw!"
  • When create succeeds and then fails on a duplicate
  • Then the captured logs hold neither "Sup3r-secret-pw!" nor any bcrypt hash starting with "$2"

docs.title: QA-042 Audit event on create and deactivate
docs.text:
• Covers: Failure Mode 3, T4
  • Type: functional
  • Given logs are captured
  • When admin1 deactivates bob
  • Then one audit event holds admin1's id, bob's id, action deactivate and a changed flag of true

docs.title: QA-043 Audit event on idempotent deactivate
docs.text:
• Covers: Failure Mode 3, T4
  • Type: edge
  • Given bob is already inactive and logs are captured
  • When admin1 deactivates bob
  • Then the audit event shows a changed flag of false

docs.title: QA-044 Login lookup down keeps login behaviour
docs.text:
• Covers: Failure Mode 4
  • Type: failure
  • Given the redis or login lookup is down
  • When any user logs in
  • Then the login behaviour equals the behaviour before this change

docs.title: QA-045 Invalid input shows no stack trace
docs.text:
• Covers: Failure Mode 5, T7
  • Type: failure
  • Given admin1 is logged in
  • When admin1 submits every invalid input from QA-011 to QA-019
  • Then each time the page shows a fixed message and no stack trace

docs.title: QA-046 Page action time
docs.text:
• Covers: Success Metric 6, T6
  • Type: performance
  • Given local Postgres holds tenant A with 100 users
  • When admin1 creates a user, lists users and deactivates a user
  • Then each action returns in under 1 second

docs.title: QA-047 Repeated create submit
docs.text:
• Covers: Edge Case 1, T7
  • Type: edge
  • Given admin1 submits the form for lena@a.example and the first call succeeded
  • When admin1 submits the same form again
  • Then the page shows "Cannot create this user." and one lena exists

docs.title: QA-048 Privilege escalation refused
docs.text:
• Covers: Success Metric 4, T6
  • Type: security
  • Given bob (role user) tries to create an admin account for himself
  • When the call runs at service level
  • Then it is refused and bob stays role user

docs.title: QA-049 Port and store stay in step
docs.text:
• Covers: Success Metric 4, T5
  • Type: functional
  • Given the user repository contract has 4 methods
  • When the conformance test compares the real store with the contract
  • Then the 4 method names and parameters match

docs.title: QA-050 Coverage and mutation gates
docs.text:
• Covers: Success Metric 5, T8
  • Type: functional

  • When the repo coverage and mutation gates run on the user service code

docs.title: QA-051 Seed script still creates users
docs.text:
• Covers: Decision (create_user signature kept)

  • Then it creates its users with the same fields as before

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The service needs a tenant-safe insert, list and actor lookup on the store. Email is unique across tenants, so a duplicate must map to one generic refusal. It serves the create and list goals and the leak-test metric.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text: In src/plugins/relational_db/postgres.py and mappers.py (signatures in the "Port signatures" section of decision.md): - mappers.py: add user_to_record(row: User) -> UserRecord. Keep user_to_dict unchanged. - insert_user(self, *, email: str, password_hash: str, role: str, name: str) -> UserRecord: take the tenant from get_current_tenant(). If empty, raise PrincipalRequiredError before any SQL. Insert the row with a new uuid4 id, the given hash and is_active = true. Catch IntegrityError and map only SQLSTATE 23505 on constraint uq_users_email to UserCreateRefusedError. Re-raise any other error unmapped. Roll back on every error. No existence pre-check. - list_users(self) -> list[UserRecord]: reuse the existing method. Change only the return annotation. Add a tenant_id predicate on top of RLS. Order by email. Return records without the hash. With no tenant set, return 0 rows. - find_active_admin(self, email: str) -> UserRecord | None: compare the email exactly (the service normalises it). Filter on the current tenant, role = 'admin' and is_active. Return None for no match. With no tenant set, return None and run no SQL. - create_user keeps its signature. The seed script still uses it. - Tests in tests/integration/test_store_users.py on real Postgres.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: An admin must deactivate users without removing the last admin, even under concurrency. The existing trigger bumps session_version, which invalidates the old cookie. It serves the deactivate goal and the concurrency edge case.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text: In src/plugins/relational_db/postgres.py, add deactivate_user(self, user_id: str, *, actor_id: str) -> bool. The service passes actor_id, which is the id of the row that find_active_admin returned. 1. Tenant from get_current_tenant(). Empty raises PrincipalRequiredError before SQL. 2. Read the target under RLS with a tenant_id predicate. A missing or foreign id raises UserNotFoundError. 3. If user_id == actor_id, raise SelfDeactivationError. This runs inside the transaction, before the last-admin check. 4. If the target is an admin, first lock the tenant's active admin rows with FOR UPDATE ORDER BY id. No LIMIT, no SKIP LOCKED, nothing else locked before. If the locked set holds the target and has one row or fewer, raise LastAdminError. An already inactive admin target is not in the locked set, so the call falls through to the guarded UPDATE and returns False. 5. If the target has role user, lock only the target. 6. UPDATE users SET is_active = false WHERE id = :id AND is_active RETURNING id. Return True for one row. Return False for zero rows (idempotent no-op). - One transaction. Roll back on error. - Import the domain errors from core.users.errors and PrincipalRequiredError from core.security. - Tests in tests/integration/test_store_deactivate.py.

docs.text:
Scenario: Foreign or unknown id
  Given a user in tenant B
  When tenant A admin deactivates that id, or a random id
  Then UserNotFoundError is raised and the row is unchanged

Scenario: Already inactive target
  Given an inactive user with session_version N
  When deactivate_user runs on it
  Then no error is raised, it returns False, and session_version is still N

Scenario: Old cookie fails
  Given an active user with session_version N
  When an admin deactivates that user
  Then it returns True, is_active is false and session_version is not N

Scenario: Self and last admin
  Given a tenant with one active admin
  When that admin deactivates self
  Then SelfDeactivationError is raised
  And when another admin is the sole active admin, deactivating that admin raises LastAdminError

Scenario: Two sessions race
  Given a tenant with exactly two active admins
  When each admin deactivates the other in two concurrent sessions
  Then exactly one active admin remains

Scenario: No tenant set
  Given no current tenant
  When deactivate_user runs
  Then PrincipalRequiredError is raised and 0 rows change

  • create_user(email, password, role, name): trim and lowercase email. Require one @, at most 256 characters, not blank. Name at most 256. Role by valid_role. Password limits as above. Every failure raises UserCreateRefusedError. Run hash_password before the insert. Call port.insert_user(email=..., password_hash=..., role=..., name=...) and return its UserRecord.
  • deactivate_user(user_id): call port.deactivate_user(user_id, actor_id=actor["id"]). The port raises UserNotFoundError, SelfDeactivationError or LastAdminError. The service lets them propagate. Emit a stdlib logging audit event with actor id, target id, action and the returned changed flag. Never log the password or the hash.

docs.title: Decision: Alembic drift test compares server defaults
Context
docs.text: The drift test calls compare_metadata with no options, so Alembic 1.20.1 does not compare server defaults. A changed model default passes silently. Alembic 1.20.1 does not compare CHECK constraints by default (name-based detection is an opt-in plugin, not enabled here). The CHECK name ck_legal_document_status would change if someone adds a naming convention with a %(constraint_name)s ck token.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Path 1: one shared options dict used by env.py and the test, conv() pins the CHECK name, and a drift test on an isolated metadata copy.
  • Path 2: inline flags in env.py, tests run command.check through env.py, and a comment plus a convention guard protect the name.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Path 1, chosen by the owner at G1. Reviewer fixes are included: - New src/data/autogen.py holds AUTOGEN_COMPARE_OPTS = {"compare_server_default": True}. It is a plain dict with no Alembic import. - migrations/env.py spreads the dict into the online context.configure. It also spreads it into the offline call, with a comment that says this is for parity only, because autogenerate does not run offline. - src/data/models.py names the CHECK conv("ck_legal_document_status"). The DDL name stays byte-identical to the plain string in migration 963e40b83003. - test_autogenerate_finds_no_changes passes opts=AUTOGEN_COMPARE_OPTS and still asserts diff == []. - A new integration test copies every table of Base.metadata with Table.to_metadata() into a fresh MetaData, so no remove_table and no missing FK target appear. It changes the status server default on the copy, flattens the nested diff, and asserts exactly 1 modify_default entry for legal_document.status. Base.metadata stays unchanged. - A new unit test builds a MetaData with naming_convention={"ck": "ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s"}, copies the table into it, and asserts the CHECK name is exactly ck_legal_document_status. - The pg_get_constraintdef test stays as the guard of the CHECK text.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The test and env.py read one dict, so their options cannot differ.
  • Accepted gap: the test does not run env.py itself. env.py has no include_object or other compare hooks today, so both runs give the same result.
  • No false drift is expected (dba): 'needs_review' is compared on the server, and 0 matches as text. The 0-diff test confirms this.
  • No migration file and no schema change.

docs.title: Requirements: Alembic drift test compares server defaults
Business Goals
docs.text:
• The drift test must catch a model server default that differs from the database. Today a changed default passes silently, and a fresh database then gets a different default than the model promises.
  • The CHECK constraint ck_legal_document_status must keep its exact name, because migrations and tests reference it by name.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• Alembic 1.20.1. MigrationContext.configure(opts={"compare_server_default": True}) turns the comparison on (alembic/runtime/migration.py:179).
  • migrations/env.py must pass compare_server_default=True in both online and offline context.configure calls, so alembic revision --autogenerate and the test use the same rule.
  • The test must use the same option source as env.py, so the two cannot drift apart.
  • Server defaults today: legal_document.status = 'needs_review', users.session_version = 0.
  • Alembic 1.20.1 does not compare CHECK constraints by default. Name-based CHECK detection needs the opt-in checkconstraint_byname plugin, which this change does not enable. The pg_get_constraintdef test stays as the guard of the CHECK text.
  • No new dependency. No schema change unless the comparison shows real drift.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL renders defaults with casts ('needs_review'::character varying). Alembic must not report this as drift.
  • A future naming_convention with a %(constraint_name)s ck token would rename the CHECK to ck_legal_document_ck_legal_document_status.
  • A model with no server default and a database column with none must give no diff.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• If the comparison gives a false positive, the drift test fails on a clean tree. Fix: a custom comparator only if a real false positive appears.
  • If someone adds a naming convention, the constraint name changes and a unit test must fail with a clear message.
  • If env.py and the test use different options, drift found by one is hidden by the other.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
• 1 new integration test: a changed model server default gives a non-empty diff (at least 1 modify_default entry).
  • The existing drift test gives 0 diff entries on the current migrations.
  • 1 unit test fails when the CHECK name in metadata is not exactly ck_legal_document_status.
  • 0 changes to existing migration files.

docs.title: Review
docs.text:
Gate: ruff check, ruff format, pyright, bandit, unit tests pass. uv lock --check passes. pip-audit could not reach the network here, CI runs it, and no dependency changed.

Verdicts: structure PASS WITH WARNINGS, security no findings, style no blockers.

Fixed: - The tests pass a copy dict(AUTOGEN_COMPARE_OPTS) to Alembic, so Alembic cannot change the shared dict. - The tests use DocumentStatus values, not string literals. - The offline comment in env.py states why the options are passed. - The users table assertion now checks the parametrized table and names the import it depends on.

Kept, with reason: - src/data/autogen.py sits next to the models. The decision chose this place, and the module has no Alembic import. - The parametrized test covers more than the decision listed (QA-008, QA-009). Each case is one more modify_default check. - The Base.metadata unchanged assertion stays in the test. It is QA-010. - _status_default_arg stays as a helper, because the type assertion needs a narrowing step.

docs.title: Path 1: single source of truth
docs.text:
• New src/data/autogen.py with AUTOGEN_COMPARE_OPTS = {"compare_server_default": True}.
  • migrations/env.py spreads it into both context.configure calls.
  • Drift test passes opts=AUTOGEN_COMPARE_OPTS to MigrationContext.configure; asserts diff == [].
  • New integration test: change the status server default on a copy of the metadata, assert at least 1 modify_default entry.
  • models.py: name=conv("ck_legal_document_status") so any naming convention keeps the name.
  • New unit test: a MetaData with a ck convention keeps the exact name.

Failure modes: one dict for env.py and the test; conv() pins the name; the drift test sees the diff list. Not handled: a cast false positive (fixed by a comparator only if seen). Effort: S. Main risk: conv() behaviour in DDL must match the plain string in migrations.

docs.title: Path 2: minimal inline
docs.text:
• migrations/env.py: add compare_server_default=True to both context.configure calls.
  • Tests run alembic.command.check(cfg), which runs env.py, so env.py is the only option source.
  • New drift test: change LegalDocument.__table__.c.status.server_default, assert command.check raises, restore in finally.
  • models.py: comment above the CHECK that the name is final.
  • Unit test: "ck" not in Base.metadata.naming_convention.

Failure modes: one option source; drift raises; a convention fails the unit test. Not handled: cast false positive; the diff list is not visible (only a raise), so the modify_default metric is weak. Effort: S. Main risk: command.check runs env.py with the advisory lock and the owner URL from the test config; the mutation of shared metadata leaks if the restore fails.

docs.title: T1: Add AUTOGEN_COMPARE_OPTS, use it in env.py and in the existing drift test
Context
docs.text: The drift test calls compare_metadata with no options, so Alembic 1.20.1 ignores server defaults. One shared options dict makes env.py and the test use the same rule. It serves the goal "catch a changed server default" and the constraint "test and env.py share one option source".

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
• Create src/data/autogen.py with AUTOGEN_COMPARE_OPTS = {"compare_server_default": True}. It is a plain dict with no Alembic import.
  • In migrations/env.py, import the dict and spread it (**AUTOGEN_COMPARE_OPTS) into the online context.configure. Spread it into the offline call too, with a comment that this is for parity only, because autogenerate does not run offline.
  • In tests/integration/test_document_status_migration.py, change test_autogenerate_finds_no_changes to call MigrationContext.configure(conn, opts=AUTOGEN_COMPARE_OPTS). Keep assert diff == [].
  • Do not edit any file in migrations/versions/.

  Then it shows 0 changes

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The login adapter, RBAC wiring and most login tests are merged. The open gaps are: no unit tests for rbac.py, no UI tests that prove a demoted or deactivated admin loses admin pages, stale ADR-0004 text, and jwt used as a transitive dependency only. See requirements.md.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Path 1: additive hardening. Tests, text scrub and a pyjwt pin. No production change.
  • Path 2: single enforcement point. UI require_admin calls core check_privilege_escalation. Removes require_role and InvalidRoleError from the public API.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Path 1, chosen by the owner at G1. Two reviewer changes apply: - Add a fail-open test for principal.require_admin_principal (principal.py), which is a third admin check. - Each demotion or deactivation test runs require_auth() with a stubbed login lookup that returns the changed row, then require_admin(). A test that edits only st.session_state["user"] proves nothing.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• No runtime behaviour changes. The public API is unchanged.
  • require_role and InvalidRoleError stay as dead code, covered only by tests. Removing them is a separate follow-up issue that needs owner approval.
  • The pyjwt pin must resolve against streamlit-authenticator 0.4.2 and pass pip-audit. If it does not, stop and report.
  • Review includes one manual mutation per guard (guard removed, test fails).

docs.title: Requirements: auth-login-ui
docs.text: The login adapter, the RBAC wiring, login throttling and most login tests are already merged. This task closes the verified gaps only. The admin UI to create and deactivate users is out of scope.

docs.title: Business Goals
docs.text:
• Maintainers get proof that a user cannot act as an admin. The MVP needs auth, RBAC and privilege-escalation tests.
  • Decided: add tests and remove drift. Add no new feature.
  • Test: every rule in src/core/security/rbac.py has a unit test that fails when the rule is removed.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• Stack: Python 3.13, streamlit 1.66.1, streamlit-authenticator 0.4.2 (ADR-0013), pytest. Quality gate: ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright, pytest.
  • src/ui/components/auth.py imports jwt to catch jwt.PyJWTError. PyJWT is only a transitive dependency of streamlit-authenticator.
  • Decided: keep the import, because CookieModel.get_cookie raises that error. Declare pyjwt as a direct, exactly pinned dependency in pyproject.toml, like the other pins.
  • Decided: remove the stale ADR-0004 mentions in src/core/security/ and the READMEs that describe it. ADR-0004 is superseded. Keep the RBAC rules of ADR-0004, and cite ADR-0013 and ADR-0003.
  • No change to the public API, the database schema or the settings.
  • Not in scope: DB-level RLS on legal_document.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• A role string that is empty, None-like, upper case ("ADMIN") or unknown must fail closed in rbac.py and in current_role().
  • An admin demoted to user, or deactivated, in the database while the session is open loses admin pages on the next rerun.
  • A cookie signed with the right key that claims a higher role still gives the database role. This is already tested. Keep it.
  • check_privilege_escalation with an unknown role raises PrivilegeEscalationError, not InvalidRoleError. Pin the present behaviour with a test.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• A denied action raises PrivilegeEscalationError (a PermissionError) in core code. In the UI it shows "Admin role required." and stops the page. No data change happens.
  • A test must fail when require_admin, is_admin or check_privilege_escalation fail open.
  • If the jwt dependency pin conflicts with streamlit-authenticator, uv pip install -e ".[dev]" fails. The task is not done until it resolves and pip-audit passes.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
• A new tests/unit/core/security/test_rbac.py covers every public name in rbac.py, and its line coverage of rbac.py is 100%.
  • At least 3 new privilege-escalation tests in the UI layer: demoted admin, deactivated admin, user calling an admin-only page. Each fails when the guard is removed (checked by one manual mutation in review).
  • 0 matches for ADR-0004 and token_store in src/core/security/. The remaining mentions in src/*/README.md are replaced or removed.
  • pyjwt is listed in pyproject.toml with an exact pin. ruff, pyright, pytest -m "not integration" and pip-audit all pass. The CI mutation gate does not drop.

docs.title: Path 1: Additive hardening
docs.text:
Lens: change no production behaviour.

  • Add tests/unit/core/security/test_rbac.py for every public name in rbac.py (100% line coverage).
  • Add 3+ UI escalation tests to tests/unit/test_ui_auth.py: demoted admin, deactivated admin, user on an admin page (DB-backed login).
  • Scrub ADR-0004 and token_store text (docstrings, comments, READMEs).
  • Add pyjwt==<resolved> to pyproject.toml.
  • Keep require_role, InvalidRoleError and check_privilege_escalation as they are. require_role and InvalidRoleError stay dead code, covered only by tests.
  • Two deciders remain: UI is_admin and core check_privilege_escalation.

Effort: S. Main risk: pyjwt pin conflict or pip-audit hit. A demoted-admin test can pass without the guard, so verify by mutation.

docs.title: Path 2: Single enforcement point
docs.text:
Lens: core/security is the only place that decides allow or deny.

  • UI require_admin calls check_privilege_escalation(current_role(), ADMIN), catches PrivilegeEscalationError, warns and stops. is_admin leaves the UI import.
  • Delete require_role and InvalidRoleError (no caller outside rbac.py and __init__.py). Update __all__ and docstrings.
  • Same tests, text scrub and pyjwt pin as path 1.
  • require_admin_principal in principal.py stays a second, separate check.

Effort: S. Main risk: removes public names, which conflicts with "no public API change" in the requirements. It needs owner sign-off. Message text "operation" must not be pinned by a test the change breaks.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Every answer needs source links and a confidence score. A low score gives "no reliable answer" and the closest sources (ADR-0008, ADR-0015). The bureaucracy agent (issue 111) and the citation UI (issue 121) consume the result. The search service (issue 96) is not built. Requirements: requirements.md.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Path 1: pure core module with frozen value types and one pure function (feasible with changes, recommended by the architect and the DBA).
  • Path 2: stored Citation table plus CitationService (not feasible for this task: it breaks three requirements and needs an answer table, RLS and a retention rule).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Path 1, with the review changes (owner choice at G1, 2026-11-27): - src/core/notices.py: NOT_LEGAL_ADVICE_NOTICE, non-empty, holds "not legal advice". - src/core/citations.py, stdlib only: - ScoredHit (frozen): source_url, quote, retrieval_score, rerank_score: float | None, and optional law, article, paragraph, document_id. - Citation (frozen): the same fields with one confidence. - Result is a tagged union: Answer(citations, confidence, notice) or NoReliableAnswer(closest_sources, notice). The refusal type has no citations and no confidence, so a caller cannot read an answer from a refusal. Callers branch with match. - decide(hits, min_confidence) -> Answer | NoReliableAnswer. - Input contract: both scores are already in [0, 1]. The search adapter (issue 96) normalizes raw scores. A bool, NaN, infinity or out-of-range value raises ValueError that names the field. The bool check runs before the number check. - Rule: no rerank score gives confidence = retrieval score. Both scores give RETRIEVAL_WEIGHT * retrieval + RERANK_WEIGHT * rerank with named constants 0.4 and 0.6. A test checks that they sum to 1.0. The weights are provisional until the evaluation runs. - Answer.citations holds only valid hits with confidence >= min_confidence, sorted by confidence descending, stable on ties. Answer.confidence is the maximum. NoReliableAnswer.closest_sources holds at most 3 valid hits by confidence descending. - A hit with an empty, non-http(s) or credential-bearing URL is dropped. - The caller passes Settings.min_confidence. The module never reads the environment. - ADR-0008 becomes accepted (front matter and index row). Its text says: Citation value object (law, article, paragraph, quote, confidence, source_url). Persistence is deferred until answers are stored. The change goes in this PR, because the issue requires it. - Issue 122 text gets a Contract section and the fix of the importer: issue 111 imports NOT_LEGAL_ADVICE_NOTICE, and issue 121 renders citations (the issue names only 121).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• No migration, no dependency, effort S. Unit tests only, with an import test for the no-I/O rule.
  • The stored citation table and the answer table wait for the answer-storage task (DBA notes: parent answer table, composite tenant FK, RLS, retention).
  • A raw-score adapter must exist before issue 96 ships, or the rule gives meaningless results.
  • Without a document version in the citation, a quote can go stale. Accepted risk.

docs.title: Types and order (lead, at refine, no design change)
docs.text:
• Answer.citations and NoReliableAnswer.closest_sources are tuple[Citation, ...]. hits is Sequence[ScoredHit].
  • Every hit's scores are validated before the URL filter drops any hit, so bad input never passes silently.

docs.title: Requirements: citations-confidence
docs.text: Source: the issue "Citations with confidence". Facts come from src/config/settings.py, src/data/models.py, docs/adr/0008-mvp-scope.md, docs/adr/0015-information-only-answers.md and docs/architecture.md.

docs.title: Business Goals
docs.text:
• Every answer shows source links and a confidence score. A low score gives "no reliable answer" and the closest sources (ADR-0008, ADR-0015). Today no citation model and no scoring rule exist.
  • The bureaucracy agent needs three things from this task: the constant NOT_LEGAL_ADVICE_NOTICE, a score for each citation, and one refusal result that holds the closest sources. It imports them and does not copy them.
  • The research and analysis agents use the same result. The citation render UI uses it too. The shared notice text lives in one place.
  • Decided (G1, 2026-11-27: path 1 with review changes): a pure core module src/core/citations.py with the citation value object, the scoring rule and the decision "answer or no reliable answer". A second module src/core/notices.py holds the notice constant.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• Python 3.13. No new dependency. No LLM call, no HTTP call and no database call inside the module.
  • The hybrid search service (issue 96) is not built. The module takes its own small input type: a source URL, a quote, a retrieval score and an optional rerank score. The search service adapts its hits to this type later.
  • Value objects follow the project style: @dataclass(frozen=True).
  • min_confidence comes from Settings.min_confidence (default 0.5, range 0.0 to 1.0). The caller passes the value in. The module does not read the environment.
  • The scoring rule is documented in the module docstring and in the ADR text. It is deterministic.
  • ADR-0008 changes from proposed to accepted in its front matter and in the index row. The ADR text is updated: the Citation entity is a value object (law, article, paragraph, confidence, source_url), not a table.
  • A table or a migration is out of scope. No answer is stored in this task.
  • Budget: 4-6 GB RAM host. The scoring uses no model.
  • Non-goals: UI, LLM answer text, search, rerank model choice, storing citations.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• Hit list is empty: the result is NoReliableAnswer with no sources.
  • Confidence exactly equal to min_confidence: normal answer (the rule is >=).
  • Confidence 0.4 with min_confidence 0.3: normal answer. With 0.5: "no reliable answer".
  • Score outside [0, 1] or not a number (NaN, infinity, bool): ValueError that names the field. The module does not clip silently.
  • Source URL empty, not http or https, or holding credentials: the hit is not a citation. It counts as "no citation".
  • Hit with no rerank score: the retrieval score is the confidence.
  • Scores are already in [0, 1]. A raw Qdrant cosine or a logit is the adapter's problem (issue 96).
  • All hits lack a valid citation: "no reliable answer". The closest sources list is empty.
  • min_confidence outside [0, 1]: ValueError.
  • Closest sources: at most 3, sorted by confidence, highest first. A tie keeps the input order.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• The module raises only ValueError for bad input. It never returns a normal answer on bad input.
  • A caller that ignores the refusal result must not show a score above the threshold as fact. The result is a union Answer | NoReliableAnswer. The refusal type has no citations and no confidence, so a caller cannot read an answer from a refusal.
  • The notice constant is never empty. A test fails when the text does not hold "not legal advice" (case-insensitive).
  • The user sees "no reliable answer" and the closest sources. The user never sees a raw score below the threshold as an answer.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
1. 100% of citations from the scorer have a valid source_url and a confidence in [0, 1] (unit test over 4 or more hit sets).
  2. 6 of 6 acceptance scenarios in the issue pass as unit tests: valid citations, below threshold, no citation, setting changes outcome, shared notice, ADR status.
  3. Boundary tests pass at confidence 0.5 (answer), 0.49 (refusal), 0.4 with threshold 0.3 (answer).
  4. The module imports no database, network or LLM package (an import test checks it).
  5. Quality gate: ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright and pytest all pass. Unit coverage of the two new modules is 100% of lines.
  6. OPEN: the weight between retrieval score and rerank score cannot be tuned before issue 96 and an evaluation exist. The first rule is fixed and documented. Risk accepted: the rule may change when the evaluation runs.

docs.title: Path 1: Pure functional core
docs.text: Core idea: src/core/citations.py holds frozen value types and one pure function decide(hits, min_confidence) -> AnswerDecision. It has no I/O import. The result carries an explicit refusal flag and the closest sources.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• src/core/notices.py: NOT_LEGAL_ADVICE_NOTICE (non-empty text, holds "not legal advice").
  • ScoredHit (frozen): source_url, quote, retrieval_score, rerank_score: float | None. The search service (issue 96) adapts its hits to this type later.
  • Citation (frozen): source_url, quote, confidence. Optional law, article, paragraph (assumption: str | None).
  • AnswerDecision (frozen): is_refusal, citations, closest_sources (at most 3), confidence, notice.
  • decide(hits, min_confidence), score(hit), is_valid_url(url).

docs.title: Scoring rule
docs.text:
• No rerank score: confidence is the retrieval score.
  • Both scores: 0.4 * retrieval + 0.6 * rerank (weights are a guess until the evaluation runs). The result stays in [0, 1].
  • Answer when the best valid confidence is >= min_confidence. Otherwise refuse.
  • Invalid URL drops the hit. Bad score or bad min_confidence raises ValueError naming the field.

docs.title: Fit and risk
docs.text:
• No table, no migration, no new dependency. Effort S.
  • Not handled: a caller that ignores is_refusal.
  • Risk: the weights are untested. A hard ValueError on one bad hit fails the request, so the adapter must send clean data.

docs.title: Path 2: Persisted entity plus service
docs.text: Core idea: Citation becomes a SQLAlchemy table in src/data/models.py with an Alembic migration. A CitationService scores hits, applies min_confidence and saves the citations of an answer through PostgreSQLStore. This is the literal reading of ADR-0008 and of the issue file list.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• Table citation: id, answer_id (plain string, no answer table exists), tenant_id, law, article, paragraph, quote, confidence (CHECK 0 to 1), source_url, created_at. Index on (tenant_id, answer_id). RLS policy on tenant_id (assumption, not verified).
  • NOT_LEGAL_ADVICE_NOTICE in src/core/notices.py.
  • RawHit, AnswerResult, and CitationService(store, min_confidence) with score, decide, save.

docs.title: Scoring rule
docs.text:
• Confidence is the rerank score when present, else the retrieval score. No blending in v1.
  • Same validation and boundary rule as path 1.

docs.title: Fit and risk
docs.text:
• Breaks three requirements: no database call in the module, no table or migration, no storing of citations.
  • Needs an answer identity, an RLS design, DB integration tests and a rewrite of the ADR text. Effort L.
  • Risk: the schema is fixed before the scoring weights and issue 96 exist. Quotes stored per tenant add a retention surface.
