docs.title: Context
docs.text: Answers need source links and a confidence score. A low score gives "no reliable answer" and the closest sources (ADR-0008, ADR-0015). This task builds the pure module that scores hits and decides. It serves the scoring, threshold, no-citation and edge-case items in requirements.md. It depends on T1 for the notice.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
Create src/core/citations.py. Stdlib and core.notices only. No environment read, no I/O. The module docstring documents the scoring rule.

Names and signatures from decision.md: - RETRIEVAL_WEIGHT = 0.4 and RERANK_WEIGHT = 0.6 (named constants, provisional). - @dataclass(frozen=True) class ScoredHit: source_url: str, quote: str, retrieval_score: float, rerank_score: float | None, and optional law, article, paragraph, document_id. - @dataclass(frozen=True) class Citation: the same fields, with one confidence: float in place of the two scores. - @dataclass(frozen=True) class Answer: citations, confidence, notice. - @dataclass(frozen=True) class NoReliableAnswer: closest_sources, notice. It has no citations and no confidence. - def decide(hits, min_confidence: float) -> Answer | NoReliableAnswer.

Rules: - Validate min_confidence in [0, 1], else ValueError. - Validate each score: the bool check runs first, then NaN, infinity and range [0, 1]. The ValueError message names the field (retrieval_score, rerank_score, min_confidence). - Confidence = retrieval score when rerank is None, else RETRIEVAL_WEIGHT * retrieval + RERANK_WEIGHT * rerank. - Drop hits whose URL is empty, not http(s), or holds credentials (userinfo). Use urllib.parse. - Sort valid hits by confidence descending (stable sort keeps input order on ties). - Keep hits with confidence >= min_confidence. If any remain: Answer(citations, confidence=max, notice=NOT_LEGAL_ADVICE_NOTICE). - Otherwise NoReliableAnswer(closest_sources=<top 3 valid hits>, notice=NOT_LEGAL_ADVICE_NOTICE). An empty list or no valid hit gives empty closest_sources. - Callers branch with match.

Resolved (lead, no design change): decision.md does not give the container types for Answer.citations and NoReliableAnswer.closest_sources, the element type of closest_sources (Citation assumed), the type of hits (Sequence[ScoredHit] assumed), or the validation point for a score on a hit that is later dropped for its URL (assumed: validate every hit first). Proposed: tuple[Citation, ...] for both fields. Decided: tuple[Citation, ...] for both fields, Sequence[ScoredHit] for hits, every hit validated before the URL filter.

Tests in tests/unit/core/test_citations.py, including an import test that checks the module imports only stdlib and core.notices (no sqlalchemy, httpx, requests, redis, celery, openai).

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Scenario: valid citations Given four or more hit sets with valid http(s) URLs and scores in [0, 1] When decide returns an Answer Then every citation has a valid source_url and a confidence in [0, 1]

Scenario: threshold boundaries Given a hit with confidence 0.5 and min_confidence 0.5 When decide runs Then the result is Answer And with confidence 0.49 and min_confidence 0.5 the result is NoReliableAnswer And with confidence 0.4 and min_confidence 0.3 the result is Answer

Scenario: no citation Given an empty hit list, or hits that all have invalid URLs When decide runs Then the result is NoReliableAnswer with empty closest_sources

docs.title: Context
docs.text: save_document and update_document accept a status from the caller, and apply_update writes any key that matches a model attribute. Any code path can approve a document without an admin check or an audit row. No migration may be added here, because the reject audit protection comes next in the same area.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Path 1: write allowlist, ignore with warning. The generic paths copy only editable fields. status has no effect and a warning names the dropped key.
  • Path 2: fail-fast contract. A status other than needs_review raises ValueError before a write. Other columns stay writable.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Path 1, chosen by the owner at G1. The architect recommended it; the DBA marked both paths feasible. - apply_update uses a fixed map from payload key to model attribute: title, content, source, source_url, is_processed map to the same name, metadata maps to metadata_, and last_updated goes through parse_dt to last_updated. It never calls setattr with a payload key. A unit test asserts that row.metadata_ is set and row.metadata is still Base.metadata. - apply_update returns the sorted names of the keys it dropped, except id. Dropped keys include status, tenant_id and unknown keys such as foo. Unknown keys were dropped silently before; they now appear in the warning on purpose. - save_document inserts with status = needs_review as a constant. The insert reads tenant_id as today (parameter, then payload, then context). - Every write path logs one warning per call that lists the dropped key names, never values: the upsert branch and update_document use the names from apply_update, and the insert branch warns when the payload has a status key. - Unknown status values (bogus, rejected, empty, None) no longer raise ValueError. They are dropped with the warning, like any other status value. - validate_status is removed, and the unused DocumentStatus import goes from mappers.py. postgres.py keeps DocumentStatus for the insert constant. The review issue adds its own approve path. - fetch.py _to_document stops sending status, so a normal ingest logs no warning. - The existing ValueError unit tests for status become unit tests of apply_update (no database) and integration tests of the store.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A save that re-sends the id of an approved row keeps it approved, and a needs_review row cannot be approved through the generic paths. The fetch task sends no id, so each fetch inserts a new needs_review row.
  • tenant_id and id can no longer change through upsert or update. This closes a move between tenants. No caller in src/ uses that route today.
  • Misuse does not raise. The warning log is the only signal.
  • Raw SQL and code outside the store can still set approved. The database-level guard (trigger or role split) is a follow-up, planned with the reject audit protection.
  • 0 migrations.

docs.title: Business Goals
docs.text:
• An admin reviews every new legal document before users see it. Today any code that calls save_document or update_document can set status to approved and skip that review, with no admin check and no audit row.
  • This change closes that path. The explicit approve method (admin check plus audit) belongs to the review issue and is out of scope here.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• Python 3.13, SQLAlchemy 2, PostgreSQL. Code in src/plugins/relational_db/postgres.py (save_document, update_document) and src/plugins/relational_db/mappers.py (apply_update, validate_status).
  • legal_document.status has the values needs_review and approved (CHECK ck_legal_document_status). Python default and server default are needs_review.
  • The only producer today is the fetch task (src/tasks/fetch.py). It sends status = needs_review.
  • No new migration, so the next migration (reject audit protection) does not have to fork from this one. A database-level guard is out of scope unless the chosen design needs it.
  • No new dependency.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• Insert through save_document with no status: the row has needs_review.
  • Insert through save_document with status = approved: the row has needs_review, or the call fails before any write. The chosen design picks one of the two.
  • Upsert through save_document of an existing approved row with status = needs_review or approved: the stored status does not change.
  • update_document with status (any value, valid or not) and other fields: the stored status does not change.
  • A status value that is not a known value (bogus, rejected, empty, None): the store must not write it. Existing tests expect ValueError for these values, and the design states whether that stays.
  • The caller's input dict is not changed by the guard. Exception: save_document still writes a generated id back into the dict (current contract).

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• If the design rejects status, the error is a ValueError raised before the store opens a session, and no row changes.
  • If the design ignores status, the store logs nothing secret and the call succeeds with the status unchanged.
  • The fetch task keeps working: an ingest saves the row as needs_review and returns saved.
  • get_document and the other read paths still return status.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
• 1 integration test: update_document(doc_id, {"status": "approved", "title": "x"}) on a needs_review row leaves status = needs_review (or raises before any write, per design). 0 status changes.
  • 1 integration test: save_document of a new payload with status = approved stores needs_review (or raises, per design).
  • 1 integration test: an upsert through save_document does not change the status of an existing row.
  • 1 integration test: the fetch task stores a new row as needs_review and logs no status warning.
  • 0 new migrations in migrations/versions/.
  • Quality gate: ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright and pytest pass. Coverage and mutation gates of CONTRIBUTING.md pass.

docs.title: Fixed in the review round
docs.text:
• Style and structure: the seven setter functions became one fixed key-to-attribute map.
  • Security (low): the warning logs the id and key names with %r, so a key cannot forge a log line.
  • Style (high, confirmed as a docstring error): the save_document docstring now states that the insert branch reports only status, and that a payload tenant_id still picks the tenant on insert.
  • Structure (medium): the migration and validate_status checks left the integration file. A unit test checks that validate_status is gone.
  • QA: 11 partial cases got integration tests.

docs.title: Kept, with reason
docs.text:
• row.metadata is Base.metadata assertion: the design requires proof that a payload key never shadows Base.metadata.
  • Insert branch reads tenant_id from the payload (security, medium): the decision keeps the current insert rule. Follow-up: take the tenant only from the argument or the context.
  • Existing-row writes do not filter by tenant (security, medium): this code predates the change, and legal_document has no RLS yet. Follow-up with the RLS work.
  • Allowlist setters check no types (security, low): a wrong type fails at commit as a database error, with no integrity break.
  • No database-level guard: the decision defers it to the reject audit protection work.

docs.title: Path 1: write allowlist, silent ignore
docs.text:
• mappers.apply_update copies only an allowlist: title, content, source, source_url, is_processed, metadata, last_updated. It skips id, status and every other key.
  • save_document inserts with status=needs_review as a constant and never reads the payload status. The upsert branch uses the allowlist.
  • update_document drops its status check. A status key has no effect.
  • validate_status loses its last caller. Delete it, or keep it for the review issue.
  • Existing ValueError tests in tests/unit/plugins/test_postgres_status.py become "status is ignored" tests.
  • Closes the general setattr route too (any model column could be written).
  • Effort: S. Risks: misuse is silent; the allowlist can drop a field a caller needs (for example tenant_id); the future approve method needs its own write path.

docs.title: Path 2: fail-fast contract
docs.text:
• New mappers.guard_status(document, *, allow_initial), called before any session. On save, a payload status other than needs_review raises ValueError. On update, any status key raises ValueError. Unknown values keep the existing ValueError.
  • save_document inserts needs_review as a constant. The upsert branch skips status, so an approved row is not demoted by a re-ingest.
  • apply_update skips status as defence in depth. Other hasattr keys still pass.
  • Fetch task needs no change: it sends needs_review. A patched payload with approved makes the task fail with ValueError.
  • Existing ValueError tests for unknown values keep passing.
  • Effort: S. Risks: callers that send status on update start to fail, even with needs_review; the future approve method needs its own write path.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Any caller can set status to approved through apply_update, which writes every key that matches a model attribute. This task replaces that with a fixed allowlist. It serves the requirements that update_document and upsert never change status, and that the caller's dict stays unchanged.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
• In src/plugins/relational_db/mappers.py, rewrite apply_update with a fixed map from payload key to model attribute: title, content, source, source_url, is_processed map to the same name, metadata maps to metadata_, last_updated goes through parse_dt to last_updated. Never call setattr with a payload key.
  • apply_update returns the sorted names of the dropped keys, except id. Dropped keys include status, tenant_id and unknown keys.
  • Do not change the input dict.
  • validate_status stays in this task (T2 removes it with its callers). Keep the file importable.
  • Rewrite the ValueError status tests in tests/unit/plugins/test_postgres_status.py as unit tests of apply_update with no database. Assert row.metadata_ is set and row.metadata is still Base.metadata.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Scenario: status is dropped Given a row with status "needs_review" When apply_update(row, {"status": "approved", "title": "x"}) runs Then row.status equals "needs_review" And row.title equals "x" And the return value equals ["status"]

Scenario Outline: any status value is dropped Given a row with status "needs_review" When apply_update(row, {"status": <value>}) runs Then row.status equals "needs_review" And the return value equals ["status"] And no error is raised Examples: | value | | "approved" | | "bogus" | | "rejected" | | "" | | None |

Scenario: tenant_id and unknown keys are dropped Given a row with tenant_id "t1" When apply_update(row, {"tenant_id": "t2", "foo": 1}) runs Then row.tenant_id equals "t1" And the return value equals ["foo", "tenant_id"]

Scenario: id is ignored and not reported Given a row with id "d1" When apply_update(row, {"id": "d2"}) runs Then row.id equals "d1" And the return value equals []

Scenario: allowed keys are copied Given a row When apply_update runs with title, content, source, source_url, is_processed, metadata and last_updated Then each value is set on the row And row.metadata_ equals the metadata value And row.metadata is still Base.metadata And the return value equals []

Scenario: input dict is unchanged Given a payload dict with "status" and "title" When apply_update(row, payload) runs Then the payload equals its copy taken before the call

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Settings (src/config/settings.py) is a plain class. Each value is a property that reads os.getenv. The issue removes the 3 Cohere rerank keys. It adds 8 keys for Qdrant, OTel, min_confidence and the local rerank model. The issue left one question OPEN: a pydantic-settings rewrite or the plain class.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: The work is size S (one module, no data or interface change), so the design-divergence flow used 2 paths, not 4. - Path 1: extend the plain class with 8 properties and one _float_in_range helper. Effort S. Reviewer: FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES. - Path 2: rewrite the class as a pydantic-settings BaseSettings. Effort L, new dependency, reads once at construction. Reviewer: FEASIBLE WITH CHANGES at high cost.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Path 1, chosen by the owner at G1. The reasons: - It keeps the requirement that a bad value fails at the first read, not at startup. - It adds no dependency, and the current tests keep the lazy-read contract. - It keeps the scope to the issue.

Reviewer changes taken into the design: - MIN_CONFIDENCE rejects inf too (5 rejection cases). - Add the 8 new keys to _ENV_KEYS in tests/unit/config/test_settings.py, so a developer .env cannot change the default tests. - Rename the section header "LLM / embeddings / reranking" and update the docstring table. Add the missing MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S row. - Add all 8 new keys to the x-app-env block of docker/docker-compose.yml. - A whitespace-only MIN_CONFIDENCE raises ValueError. - A unit test checks that the 8 new keys appear in the docstring table, docker/.env.example and the compose block. This limits the drift risk for the new keys.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The config is not typed or secret-safe the pydantic way. Secrets stay plain str.
  • The docstring table, docker/.env.example and the compose block can still drift apart for the older keys. A test checks the new keys only.
  • Owner decisions:
  • The failed-task registry settings are deferred to the registry issue.
  • An empty OTel endpoint means export off. The observability code owns the switch.
  • The commented-out Cohere block in plugins.yaml is deleted, because the issue acceptance grep covers all of src/config (found in build). The other plugin-era leftovers (RerankingPlugin) stay. They are out of scope.
  • src/config/.env.example does not exist. The PR says so.

docs.title: Business Goals
docs.text:
• Later features (Qdrant search, local rerank, confidence filter, observability) read their configuration from one place: Settings in src/config/settings.py.
  • The Cohere keys go away, because the charter replaced Cohere with a local rerank model. An operator who reads docker/.env.example must not see a Cohere key.
  • Why now: seven issues depend on these keys (search service, rerank, observability, confidence filter).
  • Decided: add the keys now, so that dependent issues do not each edit the settings file.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• Python 3.13. Settings is a plain class. Each value is a property that reads os.getenv. Validation helpers exist (_positive).
  • Remove RERANK_BASE_URL, RERANK_API_KEY, RERANK_MODEL from settings.py, docker/.env.example and the x-app-env block of docker/docker-compose.yml.
  • Add these keys with defaults:
  • QDRANT_URL = http://localhost:6333
  • QDRANT_API_KEY = empty
  • QDRANT_COLLECTION = legal_documents
  • OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT = empty (empty means export off, owner decision)
  • OTEL_SERVICE_NAME = law-by-ai
  • MIN_CONFIDENCE = 0.5
  • RERANK_MODEL_NAME = empty
  • RERANK_MODEL_PATH = empty
  • No rerank_enabled setting (owner decision in the issue).
  • Keep the LLM and embedding keys unchanged.
  • src/config/.env.example does not exist. Update only docker/.env.example. The PR says so.
  • Out of scope: the failed-task registry settings (owner decision: the registry issue adds them), the plugin-era Cohere leftovers outside src/config (RerankingPlugin), the choice of a rerank model.
  • Decided at G1: keep the plain class (Path 1). No pydantic-settings rewrite.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• MIN_CONFIDENCE that is not a number (for example abc) raises ValueError that names the variable.
  • MIN_CONFIDENCE lower than 0 or higher than 1 raises ValueError. The values 0 and 1 are valid.
  • An empty or unset variable uses its default.
  • A whitespace-only MIN_CONFIDENCE (" ") raises ValueError, the same as _int_at_least does for an integer key.
  • RERANK_MODEL_NAME and RERANK_MODEL_PATH are empty by default. Settings do not fail on empty values. The search service fails hard when it needs the model and the value is empty (that check belongs to the search issue).
  • QDRANT_URL with no scheme is accepted as a string. URL validation is the client's task.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• A bad MIN_CONFIDENCE value fails at first read with a ValueError. It never falls back silently to the default.
  • An old .env file that still sets RERANK_BASE_URL does no harm: no code reads it.
  • An empty OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT means no export. The app starts with no collector. The app observability code owns this switch: it configures an exporter only when the setting is not empty. It does not rely on the OTel SDK default (localhost:4317).
  • No secret value appears in a log or an error message. Error messages name the variable, not the value, for QDRANT_API_KEY.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
• grep -riE 'cohere|rerank_base_url|rerank_api_key' src/config docker/.env.example returns 0 lines.
  • RERANK_ keys in docker/docker-compose.yml: only RERANK_MODEL_NAME and RERANK_MODEL_PATH (2 lines).
  • Settings has 0 attributes named rerank_enabled, rerank_base_url, rerank_api_key or rerank_model.
  • A unit test checks that each of the 8 new keys appears in the Settings docstring table, in docker/.env.example and in the compose x-app-env block.
  • Each of the 8 new keys has a default test and an override test: at least 16 unit cases.
  • MIN_CONFIDENCE has at least 5 rejection cases: abc, -0.1, 1.1, nan, inf. Surrounding whitespace (0.5) is accepted.
  • Gate: ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright, fast tests, diff-cover 90% or more on changed lines. The CI mutation gate covers only src/agents/fetch/, so it does not apply to this change.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text: Settings stays a plain class. Each new key is one @property over os.getenv, in the current style. Delete rerank_base_url, rerank_api_key and rerank_model. Add three sections: Qdrant, Observability, Rerank (local).

docs.title: New properties
docs.text:
• qdrant_url: QDRANT_URL, default http://localhost:6333. The property does not validate the URL.
  • qdrant_api_key: QDRANT_API_KEY, default empty.
  • qdrant_collection: QDRANT_COLLECTION, default legal_documents.
  • otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, default empty. Empty means export off.
  • otel_service_name: OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, default law-by-ai.
  • min_confidence: _float_in_range("MIN_CONFIDENCE", 0.5, 0.0, 1.0).
  • rerank_model_name and rerank_model_path: default empty. An empty value does not fail.

docs.title: New helper
docs.text: _float_in_range(name: str, default: float, minimum: float, maximum: float) -> float - An empty or unset variable gives default. - A value that is not a number raises ValueError that names the variable. - A value outside [minimum, maximum] raises ValueError. The check not (minimum <= value <= maximum) also rejects nan and inf. The values 0 and 1 stay valid. - The error message shows the raw value. This is acceptable because MIN_CONFIDENCE is not a secret. Only non-secret keys use the helper.

docs.title: Files touched
docs.text:
• src/config/settings.py: the properties, the helper and the docstring table (remove 3 rows, add 8).
  • docker/.env.example: remove the 3 Cohere keys, add the 8 new keys.
  • docker/docker-compose.yml x-app-env: remove the 3 old RERANK_* keys, add the 8 new keys.
  • tests/unit/config/test_settings.py: default and override cases for each new key, plus the rejection cases abc, -0.1, 1.1, nan and the boundary values 0 and 1.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text:
• A bad MIN_CONFIDENCE raises ValueError at the first read. Reads are lazy, the same as _positive.
  • An old .env with RERANK_BASE_URL does no harm, because no code reads it.
  • An empty OTLP endpoint returns "". The consumer treats it as export off.
  • There is no fail-fast check at startup. This matches the current behavior.

docs.title: Effort
docs.text: S. About 8 properties, one helper of about 12 lines, 3 deletions and the config files.

docs.title: Main risk
docs.text: The docstring table, .env.example and the compose block can drift apart, because no single source of truth exists. The success-metric greps check only the removal.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
• Rewrite Settings as a pydantic_settings.BaseSettings with typed fields and no env prefix. The about 70 current keys become fields with their current defaults.
  • min_confidence is a float field with a field_validator. The validator rejects non-numbers, values below 0, values above 1 and nan. The error names the variable and does not show the value.
  • Secrets such as QDRANT_API_KEY become SecretStr.
  • Derived values (postgres_url, redis_url, celery_*, the pool config) stay as properties.
  • The model config sets extra="ignore", env_ignore_empty=True and hide_input_in_errors=True.
  • Remove the 3 Cohere keys and add the 8 new keys.

docs.title: Lazy reads and current tests
docs.text:
• Today each property reads os.getenv at each access. A BaseSettings reads the environment once, at construction. This breaks the lazy-read contract.
  • The tests that call monkeypatch.setenv after construction must clear get_settings or build a new Settings(). There are 6 test files in tests/unit/config/.
  • A bad MIN_CONFIDENCE then fails at construction, so it breaks startup for every caller, also for callers that never read it. This differs from the requirement "fails at first read".

docs.title: Files touched
docs.text:
• pyproject.toml and the lockfile: add pydantic-settings (new dependency).
  • src/config/settings.py: a full rewrite. Field constraints replace _positive and _int_at_least.
  • docker/.env.example and docker/docker-compose.yml: the same key changes as Path 1.
  • All 6 test files in tests/unit/config/, plus the new cases.
  • Possibly call sites that use Settings() directly.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text:
• A bad MIN_CONFIDENCE raises ValidationError, which is a subclass of ValueError.
  • An old RERANK_BASE_URL does no harm, because of extra="ignore".
  • By default, a pydantic error message shows the input value. hide_input_in_errors=True is necessary to keep secrets out of error messages.

docs.title: Effort
docs.text: L. A rewrite of 602 lines, a new dependency and a change to the test contract in 6 files.

docs.title: Main risk
docs.text: The read-once behavior changes the contract that all current tests rely on. Other risks: an error message that shows a secret if the config is wrong, and a Docker image rebuild for the new dependency.

docs.title: T1: Settings properties, helper, docstring table, unit tests
Context
docs.text: Later features (Qdrant search, local rerank, confidence filter, observability) read their configuration from Settings. The charter replaced Cohere with a local rerank model, so the three Cohere keys must go. This task changes settings.py and its unit tests. It serves the business goals and the Edge Cases and Failure Modes of requirements.md.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
Path 1 of decision.md: extend the plain class. Each value is a property that reads os.getenv on each access.

In src/config/settings.py: - Remove the properties rerank_base_url, rerank_api_key, rerank_model and their three rows in the module docstring table. Before the removal, run grep -rnE 'rerank_base_url|rerank_api_key|rerank_model\b' src tests. Discovery found no reader outside src/config/settings.py. Stop and report if a reader exists. - Add a helper _float_in_range(name, default, low, high), next to _int_at_least. An unset or empty value gives the default. A value that has only whitespace raises ValueError. It strips surrounding whitespace, then converts to float. It rejects a non-number, nan, inf, and a value outside low..high (both ends valid). Every error message names the variable. - Add 8 properties with these env keys and defaults: - qdrant_url = QDRANT_URL, http://localhost:6333 (plain string, no scheme check) - qdrant_api_key = QDRANT_API_KEY, empty - qdrant_collection = QDRANT_COLLECTION, legal_documents - otel_exporter_otlp_endpoint = OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, empty (empty means export off) - otel_service_name = OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, law-by-ai - min_confidence = MIN_CONFIDENCE, 0.5, uses _float_in_range(..., 0.0, 1.0) - rerank_model_name = RERANK_MODEL_NAME, empty - rerank_model_path = RERANK_MODEL_PATH, empty - For string keys, an empty variable uses the default. Settings never fail on an empty RERANK_MODEL_NAME or RERANK_MODEL_PATH. - Do not add rerank_enabled. - Rename the section header "LLM / embeddings / reranking (ADR-0014)" to match the new content. Put the Qdrant, OTel, min_confidence and rerank model properties under clear headers. - Update the docstring table: add the 8 new rows and the missing MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S row (default 300). - No secret value in an error message. QDRANT_API_KEY has no validation, so no message names its value.

In tests/unit/config/test_settings.py: - Add the 8 new keys to _ENV_KEYS. - Add a default test and an override test for each of the 8 keys (at least 16 cases). - Add MIN_CONFIDENCE rejection cases (abc, -0.1, 1.1, nan, inf, " ") that check ValueError and that the message contains MIN_CONFIDENCE. Add accept cases (0, 1, 0.5) and an empty-value case. - Add a test that Settings has none of rerank_enabled, rerank_base_url, rerank_api_key, rerank_model. - Add test_old_rerank_keys_do_no_harm: with RERANK_BASE_URL, RERANK_API_KEY and RERANK_MODEL set, reading the 8 new properties raises no error.

docs.title: T2: Env example, compose block and drift test
Context
docs.text: An operator reads docker/.env.example and the compose x-app-env block to learn the keys. Cohere keys there would mislead them, and the 8 new keys must be visible. This task serves the business goal "no Cohere key in docker/.env.example" and the success metrics on grep counts and the drift test. It depends on T1, because the drift test reads the Settings docstring table.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
In docker/.env.example: - Remove RERANK_BASE_URL, RERANK_API_KEY, RERANK_MODEL (lines under the embedding keys). - Add the 8 new keys with their defaults: QDRANT_URL=http://localhost:6333, QDRANT_API_KEY=, QDRANT_COLLECTION=legal_documents, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=, OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=law-by-ai, MIN_CONFIDENCE=0.5, RERANK_MODEL_NAME=, RERANK_MODEL_PATH=. Use short comments. State that an empty OTel endpoint means export off. - Fix the header comment "LLM / embeddings / reranking" so it does not promise a remote rerank service.

In docker/docker-compose.yml, block x-app-env: - Remove RERANK_BASE_URL:, RERANK_API_KEY:, RERANK_MODEL:. - Add the 8 new keys as bare keys (NAME:), the style of the neighbouring optional settings. - grep -c 'RERANK_' docker/docker-compose.yml must print 2.

New file tests/unit/config/test_settings_drift.py: - One parametrized test over the 8 new keys. docs.title: Decision: last-admin backstop and admin action audit
Context
docs.text: The last-admin rule lives in the store only. Direct SQL and future paths (reactivate, role change) can leave a tenant with no admin. The admin actions are only a structured log event.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: The solution-architect and the DBA reviewed the design. Both agree on the points below.

docs.title: Trigger
docs.text:
• One migration revision, down_revision = "81dde4a27be7".
  • Function public.users_guard_last_admin(), plpgsql, SECURITY INVOKER, owner lawbyai_owner, SET search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp, every name schema-qualified, no EXECUTE for PUBLIC.
  • Trigger trg_users_last_admin: BEFORE UPDATE OF is_active, role, tenant_id OR DELETE ON users FOR EACH ROW.
  • The body acts only when OLD is an active admin and the change removes it (delete, demotion, deactivation, tenant move).
  • It locks the other active admins of OLD.tenant_id with FOR NO KEY UPDATE in id order. If it finds none, it raises SQLSTATE 23514 with CONSTRAINT = 'trg_users_last_admin'.
  • Why invoker: RLS shows the session every admin of the tenant it can change, so a DEFINER function adds nothing. Why row locks and not a tenant-row mutex: row locks stay correct under REPEATABLE READ, which fails with 40001.
  • Owner bypass: current_user = 'lawbyai_owner' and app.skip_last_admin_check = 'on'. The app role cannot use it. Test helpers that run as the owner set it.

docs.title: Audit table
docs.text:
• admin_action_audit(id bigint identity, tenant_id, actor_id, action, target_id, created_at timestamptz default now()). No foreign keys, so rows outlive users. CHECK on action.
  • RLS enabled and forced, tenant-only policy with WITH CHECK. lawbyai_app gets SELECT and INSERT only. The rows are kept forever.
  • Writer: the store, in the same transaction as the action. A trigger cannot see the actor id without a spoofable session setting. The service already resolves the actor id.
  • The store write is a separate commit after the schema commit. Another session edits the same files, so that commit is rebased last.

docs.title: Downgrade
docs.text: Drop the trigger, the function, then the table. It stops with an error if the audit table holds rows.

docs.title: Requirements: last-admin backstop and admin action audit
Business Goals
docs.text:
• A tenant always keeps at least one active admin. The rule holds for every writer, not only for PostgreSQLStore.deactivate_user.
  • Every admin user action (create user, deactivate user) leaves an audit row that the app role cannot change or delete.
  • The actor in the audit row is the active admin row of the request principal. A caller cannot write another actor.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL, Alembic, three roles (lawbyai_owner, lawbyai_app, lawbyai_auth). Alembic runs as lawbyai_owner.
  • users has FORCE row level security with a tenant-only policy. A session sees and changes only rows of app.current_tenant.
  • A new revision follows 81dde4a27be7. It does not edit frozen revisions.
  • deactivate_user already locks the active admins in id order and raises LastAdminError first. The trigger is the backstop.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• A direct UPDATE that sets is_active = false or role <> 'admin' on the last active admin: refused.
  • A DELETE of the last active admin: refused.
  • A tenant_id change of the last active admin (moves the admin out of the tenant): refused.
  • One statement that changes all admins of a tenant: the last row is refused, so the statement fails as a whole.
  • A change that leaves another active admin, or a change of a user or an inactive admin: allowed.
  • Two sessions that remove two different admins at once: one waits, then is refused or aborted. The tenant never reaches zero.
  • Owner maintenance (test cleanup, a tenant purge): the owner may skip the check with the transaction setting app.skip_last_admin_check = 'on'. The trigger ignores the setting for every other role.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Two raw SQL sessions can deadlock (SQLSTATE 40P01). PostgreSQL aborts one. The invariant holds. The store path does not deadlock because it locks in id order.
  • A superuser bypasses RLS and the check sees all rows. A lawbyai_owner session with no tenant sees no rows and is refused (fail closed).
  • A downgrade that drops the audit table would lose audit data. It stops when the table holds rows.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Agents need one client to call an OpenAI-compatible server, with a base URL, model, timeout and API key per agent. Settings already has LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_API_KEY, LLM_MODEL and seven LLM_MODEL_<AGENT> properties. It has no timeout and no per-agent URL or key. Requirements: requirements.md.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Path 1: Settings resolves the full per-agent config over a closed tuple. config would import the error from core (feasible with changes).
  • Path 2: a ChatModel port, an LLMClient adapter and a resolver in src/core/llm/. Settings gets only a generic lookup (feasible with changes, recommended by the architect).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Path 2, with the review changes (owner choice at G1, 2026-11-23): - src/core/llm/config.py holds an explicit LLM_AGENTS tuple of the seven names, AgentLLMConfig (frozen: base_url, model, timeout, api_key) and resolve(settings, agent_name). A test checks the tuple against the seven llm_model_* properties. - Settings adds llm_setting(field, agent): LLM_<FIELD>_<AGENT>, then LLM_<FIELD>. It adds llm_timeout (LLM_TIMEOUT, default 60 s, positive float, else ValueError naming the variable). resolve raises ValueError that names LLM_TIMEOUT_<AGENT> for a bad per-agent value. Existing properties stay. Settings raises only ValueError. - src/core/llm/ports.py: ChatModel Protocol, chat(agent_name, messages) -> str. - src/core/llm/errors.py: LLMError(message, status_code=None) and LLMTimeoutError(LLMError). LLMConfigError is separate (base Exception), so a caller that catches LLMError does not treat config as transport. - src/core/llm/client.py: LLMClient(settings, *, transport=None), the only public name. It follows the Mistral adapter (follow_redirects=False, trust_env=False, no logging), streams the body with a 1 MiB cap and a monotonic deadline checked before each read and after each chunk, and passes httpx.Timeout(timeout / 4) to the request. Worst case is about 1.25 × timeout. A single slow read gets at most timeout / 4. (Changed after G1 by the owner: httpx limits each phase separately, so a bound of timeout + 1 s is not possible without a thread.) Errors never hold the key, the content or the base URL. A base URL with credentials, a query, a fragment, or a scheme other than http/https raises LLMConfigError that names the agent, and no request is sent. http:// stays allowed for local servers. A configured key needs https:// unless the host is loopback (localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1), else LLMConfigError naming the agent (added after G1 from the PR review). A key with a non-ASCII or non-printable character raises LLMConfigError. With LLM_BASE_URL unset, the base URL defaults to http://localhost:11434/v1. A trailing / is stripped before the join. - The issue Gherkin names change to bureaucracy_assistant and document_processor, and the issue gets a Contract section.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Config stays a leaf module. Agent tests can use a fake ChatModel.
  • A typo in a per-agent env name falls back to the global value without a warning. Accepted risk.
  • A new agent needs one name in LLM_AGENTS and one llm_model_* property.
  • Effort S-M: about 40 lines in Settings, four new small modules and their unit tests.

docs.title: Hardening (2026-11-27, owner decision)
docs.text:
• Hard deadline: a network backend clips every socket operation to the time left. Worst case is about 1 x timeout on the real transport. A per-call ContextVar carries the deadline, so pooled connections use the deadline of the current call.
  • Traceback locals: chat re-raises with no inner frames and without its arguments, so a logger that prints locals sees no secret.
  • Connection reuse: one lazy httpx.Client per LLMClient, with close() and context-manager support. The timeout is passed per request, because agents have different timeouts.

docs.title: Requirements: llm-client
docs.text: Source: issue "OpenAI-compatible LLM client". Facts come from src/config/settings.py, src/agents/fetch/ocr/mistral.py and the httpx docs.

docs.title: Business Goals
docs.text:
• Each agent calls its own model on a local OpenAI-compatible server through one client. Today no client exists, so no agent can call a model.
  • The client unblocks the agent work in milestone "Phase 5 - Agents".
  • Decided: one shared client, LLMClient.chat(agent_name, messages) -> str, in src/core/llm/client.py.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• Python 3.13, httpx==0.28.1 (already a main dependency). No new dependency.
  • Settings stay a plain class with lazy os.getenv properties. Invalid values raise ValueError that names the variable.
  • Per agent: base URL, model, timeout, API key. Each falls back to a global value: LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_MODEL, LLM_TIMEOUT, LLM_API_KEY.
  • The existing LLM_MODEL_<AGENT> variables and the seven agent names stay valid (document_fetcher, document_processor, legal_research, change_tracker, knowledge_graph, analysis, bureaucracy_assistant).
  • Request: POST {base_url}/chat/completions with body {"model", "messages"}. Strip a trailing / from base_url before the join. Answer: choices[0].message.content.
  • Follow the Mistral OCR adapter: follow_redirects=False, trust_env=False, injectable transport, no log line with the key or the message content.
  • Budget: 4-6 GB RAM host. The client holds no model and adds no background thread.
  • Non-goals: streaming, tool calls, model choice, retries.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• Unknown agent name: chat raises LLMConfigError that names the agent. No HTTP request is sent.
  • Agent with no model (empty per-agent and global value): LLMConfigError that names the agent and the variable.
  • Empty messages list: ValueError before any request.
  • Response body larger than 1 MiB: LLMError (fixed cap, not configurable).
  • Agent names are the seven code names. The issue Gherkin uses bureaucracy_assistant and document_processor (owner decision at G1, no alias).
  • Base URL with credentials, a query, a fragment, or a scheme other than http/https: LLMConfigError that names the agent. No request is sent.
  • API key set with a plain http:// base URL to a non-loopback host: LLMConfigError that names the agent. No request is sent.
  • API key with a non-ASCII or non-printable character: LLMConfigError that names the agent and does not hold the key.
  • LLM_BASE_URL unset: the base URL is http://localhost:11434/v1.
  • Empty API key: the client sends no Authorization header.
  • Response with no choices, or a non-string content, or non-JSON body: LLMError (status 200 kept on the error).
  • Timeout value not a positive number: ValueError from Settings or resolve that names the variable.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Server slower than the timeout: LLMTimeoutError (subclass of LLMError) within 1.25 × timeout + 1 s. httpx limits each phase separately, so each phase (pool, connect, write, read) gets timeout / 4 and a monotonic deadline is checked between body chunks (owner decision after G1, 2026-11-23).
  • HTTP status not 2xx: LLMError with status_code. The error text holds no API key, no message content and no base URL.
  • Connection refused or other transport error: LLMError with status_code=None.
  • The client never retries. The caller (a Celery task) decides what to do (ADR-0006 stores failed tasks).

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
• 5 of 5 Gherkin scenarios of the issue pass as unit tests with httpx.MockTransport.
  • Timeout test: chat raises within 1.25 × timeout + 1 s (1.25 s for the 0.2 s test timeout). A stall after one chunk is covered.
  • Line coverage of src/core/llm/ is 100 % in unit tests. Diff coverage meets the CONTRIBUTING.md gate.
  • Quality gate: ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright, pytest all pass with 0 errors.
  • 0 occurrences of the API key value and the base URL in any raised error text (checked by a test).

docs.title: Review: llm-client
docs.text: Verdict: PASS WITH WARNINGS (2026-11-23, range origin/main..feature/llm-client). Final architect review: CLEAR.

docs.title: Gate
docs.text: ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright (0 errors), bandit, pytest -m "not integration" (1830 passed), total coverage 98.88 %, diff coverage 100 %. TDD order: pass. uv lock --check failed only in the sandbox cache (pyproject.toml and uv.lock unchanged). pip-audit, mutation testing and the Docker integration suite run in CI (a local hook blocks the Docker env file).

docs.title: Fixed in review
docs.text:
• The AgentLLMConfig repr hides the key and the base URL.
  • httpx.InvalidURL is wrapped into a secret-free LLMError. The base URL check rejects a missing host or a bad port.
  • Accept-Encoding: identity is sent, so the 1 MiB cap counts wire bytes.
  • Timeout errors name the variable but not the value. One shared validator, positive_float. Settings.llm_var_name and Settings.llm_agent_timeout own the env naming, and core.llm reads no env.
  • After CodeRabbit: a compressed response is rejected before it is read, deeply nested JSON is a malformed response, a base URL with ? or # is rejected, and a key needs https for a non-loopback host.
  • After the final architect review: LLM_BASE_URL defaults to http://localhost:11434/v1, and a key with a non-ASCII or non-printable character is a config error.
  • Named _HTTPX_PHASES, a flat _parse_content, __all__, and behavior names for tests.
  • Timeout bound: each httpx phase gets timeout / 4 (owner decision after G1).

docs.title: Warnings kept
docs.text:
• Closed (2026-11-27, owner decision): medium, perf: a new httpx.Client for each call. LLMClient now makes one client on first use and reuses it. close() and the context manager free it, and the next call opens a new one.
  • low, security: http:// is allowed without a key for any host. A key needs https unless the host is loopback. There is no host allowlist. URLs come only from the environment.
  • low, security: trust_env=False ignores custom CA bundles. Add an explicit setting when a private CA is needed.
  • Closed (2026-11-27, owner decision): medium, availability (CodeRabbit): header trickle past the deadline. The real transport now uses an httpcore network backend that clips each connect, TLS handshake, read and write to the time left before the call deadline, so a trickle ends at about 1 x timeout. No thread and no new dependency. A custom transport gets no such clip and must enforce its own deadline: a header trickle can hold it with no upper bound. Writes go in 4 KiB slices, and each slice gets the time left. The fix sets the private HTTPTransport._pool, because httpx takes no network backend argument: check it on each httpx upgrade.
  • low, structure: the module-level clock _now is patched in tests instead of being injected.
  • low, structure: settings.py and test_settings.py were over 500 lines before this change.
  • QA-046 partial: memory growth is not measured. The thread count is checked.
  • Closed (2026-11-27, docs PR review): a raised error kept the chat frame, whose locals held the key, the base URL and the messages. chat now drops the traceback of the inner frames and deletes its arguments before the raise. A test walks tb_frame.f_locals over the whole traceback.

docs.title: Path 1: Closed registry, settings-owned
docs.text: Core idea: Settings owns all LLM config resolution over a fixed tuple of the seven agent names. LLMClient is a thin class that asks Settings for a frozen config and does the HTTP call.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• LLM_AGENTS: tuple[str, ...] in settings.py (closed registry).
  • LLMAgentConfig frozen dataclass: base_url, model, timeout, api_key.
  • Settings.llm_agent_config(agent: str) -> LLMAgentConfig.
  • Settings.llm_timeout (LLM_TIMEOUT), positive float.
  • LLMClient(settings, transport: httpx.BaseTransport | None = None).chat(agent_name, messages) -> str.
  • src/core/llm/errors.py: LLMError(msg, status_code=None), LLMTimeoutError(LLMError), LLMConfigError.

docs.title: Interfaces
docs.text:
• Per field: LLM_<FIELD>_<AGENT>, then global LLM_<FIELD>. LLM_MODEL_<AGENT> already fits.
  • The seven llm_model_<agent> properties become wrappers over llm_agent_config(...).model.
  • Unknown agent or empty model: LLMConfigError naming the agent (and the variable).
  • Bad timeout: ValueError naming the variable.
  • Settings imports LLMConfigError from core.llm (config depends on core).

docs.title: Error mapping
docs.text:
Case Result Unknown agent LLMConfigError, no request Empty messages ValueError, no request Empty API key no Authorization header httpx.TimeoutException LLMTimeoutError Other httpx.HTTPError LLMError(status_code=None) Non-2xx LLMError(status_code=n), no key or body in text Bad 200 body LLMError(status_code=200)

Mistral pattern: follow_redirects=False, trust_env=False, injected transport, no logging, no retries, a monotonic deadline across the streamed read so the total stays within timeout + 1 s.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: src/config/settings.py, new src/core/llm/{__init__,client,errors}.py, client and settings unit tests, .env.example.

docs.title: Effort and risks
docs.text:
Effort M (settings tests cover 7 agents x 4 fields). 1. A new agent needs a settings edit, and the registry can drift from the model properties. 2. config depends on core for the error type. 3. A typo in one of 28 per-agent variables falls back to the global value silently.

Choose it when the agent set is stable and validation should live in one place.

docs.title: Path 2: Hexagonal port, open convention
docs.text: Core idea: agents depend on a ChatModel Protocol. An OpenAICompatibleClient adapter implements it. A convention resolver builds env names from the agent name (LLM_<FIELD>_<AGENT>, then LLM_<FIELD>).

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• src/core/llm/ports.py: ChatModel Protocol, chat(agent_name, messages) -> str.
  • errors.py: LLMError(msg, status_code=None), LLMConfigError(LLMError), LLMTimeoutError(LLMError).
  • config.py: AgentLLMConfig frozen dataclass and resolve(settings, agent_name).
  • client.py: OpenAICompatibleClient(settings, *, transport=None), alias LLMClient.
  • settings.py: generic llm_setting(field, agent), llm_timeout, known_llm_agents() derived from llm_model_* property names. Existing properties untouched.

docs.title: Flow and errors
docs.text:
• Empty messages: ValueError. Unknown agent (not in allow-list) or empty model: LLMConfigError, no request.
  • httpx.TimeoutException -> LLMTimeoutError, plus a monotonic deadline across the read.
  • Other httpx.HTTPError -> LLMError(status_code=None). Non-2xx (redirects too) -> LLMError(status_code=n). Bad 200 body -> LLMError(status_code=200).
  • No key or content in error text, no logging, trust_env=False, follow_redirects=False.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: New src/core/llm/{__init__,ports,errors,config,client}.py and tests. Edited src/config/settings.py (about 40 lines), .env.example.

docs.title: Effort and risks
docs.text:
Effort S-M. 1. Generic env lookup: an env-name typo falls back to the global value silently. 2. Allow-list from property-name introspection is brittle on rename. 3. The port has one implementation, so it is ceremony until a second backend exists. It does let agents test against a fake ChatModel.

Choose it when agents are added often and agent tests need a fake model.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The LLM client needs a per-agent value with a global fallback for base URL, model, timeout and API key. Settings has LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_API_KEY, LLM_MODEL and seven LLM_MODEL_<AGENT> properties. It has no timeout and no generic lookup. This task adds both. It serves the "Per agent" constraint and the timeout edge case of requirements.md.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
Path 2 of decision.md: Settings gets only a generic lookup. In src/config/settings.py: - Add method llm_setting(self, field: str, agent: str) -> str. It reads LLM_<FIELD>_<AGENT> (field and agent upper-cased), then LLM_<FIELD>. A set non-empty value wins. It returns "" when both are unset or empty. - Add property llm_timeout -> float. Key LLM_TIMEOUT, default 60.0. Surrounding whitespace is stripped. An empty value gives the default. A non-number, nan, inf, zero or a negative value raises ValueError. The message contains LLM_TIMEOUT. - Keep the seven llm_model_* properties, llm_model, llm_base_url and llm_api_key unchanged. - Settings raises only ValueError. It does not import from src/core.

In tests/unit/config/test_settings.py: add the keys LLM_TIMEOUT, LLM_BASE_URL_BUREAUCRACY_ASSISTANT and the other keys the new tests use to _ENV_KEYS. Add one case per scenario below.

Decided (default kept): Does llm_setting strip whitespace from string values (model, URL, key)? The decision names no rule. Default in this spec is no strip.

docs.text:
Scenario: The per-agent value wins over the global value
  Given LLM_MODEL is "global-m" and LLM_MODEL_BUREAUCRACY_ASSISTANT is "agent-m"
  When the code calls llm_setting("model", "bureaucracy_assistant")
  Then the result is "agent-m"

Scenario: The global value is the fallback
  Given LLM_MODEL is "global-m" and LLM_MODEL_DOCUMENT_PROCESSOR is not set
  When the code calls llm_setting("model", "document_processor")
  Then the result is "global-m"

Scenario: Both values unset
  Given LLM_API_KEY and LLM_API_KEY_DOCUMENT_PROCESSOR are not set
  When the code calls llm_setting("api_key", "document_processor")
  Then the result is the empty string

Scenario: The timeout has a default
  Given LLM_TIMEOUT is not set
  When the code reads llm_timeout
  Then the value is 60.0

Scenario: The timeout accepts a padded number
  Given LLM_TIMEOUT is " 0.2 "
  When the code reads llm_timeout
  Then the value is 0.2

Scenario Outline: The timeout rejects a bad value
  Given LLM_TIMEOUT is <value>
  When the code reads llm_timeout
  Then a ValueError is raised
  And the error message contains "LLM_TIMEOUT"
  Examples:
    | value |
    | abc   |
    | 0     |
    | -1    |
    | nan   |
    | inf   |

Scenario: Existing model properties are unchanged
  Given LLM_MODEL_BUREAUCRACY_ASSISTANT is "m1"
  When the code reads llm_model_bureaucracy_assistant
  Then the value is "m1"

docs.title: T2: src/core/llm errors, port and config resolver
Context
docs.text: The client needs error types, a port for fakes and a resolver that builds one frozen config per agent. This keeps config a leaf module and lets agent tests use a fake ChatModel. It serves the Edge Cases and Failure Modes of requirements.md.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
Path 2 of decision.md. New package src/core/llm/. __init__.py stays empty of public names except as needed by T3.

errors.py: - class LLMError(Exception) with __init__(self, message: str, status_code: int | None = None). It keeps status_code as an attribute. - class LLMTimeoutError(LLMError). - class LLMConfigError(Exception). Its base is Exception, not LLMError.

ports.py: - class ChatModel(Protocol) with def chat(self, agent_name: str, messages: list[dict[str, str]]) -> str: .... - The Protocol method body ... carries # pragma: no cover, because no code runs it and T3 needs 100 % coverage of src/core/llm.

config.py: - LLM_AGENTS: tuple[str, ...] = document_fetcher, document_processor, legal_research, change_tracker, knowledge_graph, analysis, bureaucracy_assistant. - @dataclass(frozen=True) class AgentLLMConfig with fields base_url: str, model: str, timeout: float, api_key: str. - def resolve(settings: Settings, agent_name: str) -> AgentLLMConfig: - Unknown agent: LLMConfigError, message contains the agent name. - Values come from settings.llm_setting for base_url, model, timeout, api_key. The timeout falls back to settings.llm_timeout. - Empty model: LLMConfigError, message contains the agent name and the variable LLM_MODEL_<AGENT>. - Bad per-agent timeout (not a positive finite number): ValueError, message contains LLM_TIMEOUT_<AGENT>. - Base URL with credentials, a query, a fragment, or a scheme other than http/https: LLMConfigError, message contains the agent name. The message holds no URL. - Order of checks is not fixed by the decision.

Tests: tests/unit/core/llm/test_errors.py, test_config.py. A test compares LLM_AGENTS with the set of llm_model_* properties found on Settings by dir. A test file defines a fake class and assigns it to a ChatModel variable, so pyright checks it.

Decided (default kept): Is an empty base URL (no per-agent and no global value) an LLMConfigError? The decision names only the URL checks. Default in this spec: yes, same error, names the agent. Decided (default kept): Exact message texts are not in decision.md. Only the rule "names the agent" and "names the variable" is fixed.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Scenario: Error hierarchy

  Then LLMTimeoutError is a subclass of LLMError
  And LLMConfigError is not a subclass of LLMError

  And LLMError("x").status_code is None

Scenario: LLM_AGENTS matches Settings
  Given the Settings class
  Then LLM_AGENTS equals the set of names behind the seven llm_model_* properties

Scenario: A per-agent value wins
  Given LLM_BASE_URL_BUREAUCRACY_ASSISTANT is "http://a:1/v1" and LLM_BASE_URL is "http://g:2/v1"
  And LLM_MODEL_BUREAUCRACY_ASSISTANT is "m-a" and LLM_TIMEOUT_BUREAUCRACY_ASSISTANT is "5"
  And LLM_API_KEY_BUREAUCRACY_ASSISTANT is "k-a"

  Then the config is base_url "http://a:1/v1", model "m-a", timeout 5.0, api_key "k-a"

Scenario: Unknown agent

  And the message contains "nope"

Scenario: No model
  Given no model variable is set for document_processor
  When the code calls resolve(settings, "document_processor")
  Then LLMConfigError is raised
  And the message contains "document_processor" and "LLM_MODEL_DOCUMENT_PROCESSOR"

Scenario: Bad per-agent timeout
  Given LLM_TIMEOUT_BUREAUCRACY_ASSISTANT is "0"
  When the code calls resolve(settings, "bureaucracy_assistant")
  Then ValueError is raised
  And the message contains "LLM_TIMEOUT_BUREAUCRACY_ASSISTANT"

Scenario Outline: Bad base URL

  And the message contains "bureaucracy_assistant"

    | http://host/v1#frag      |
    | ftp://host/v1            |

Scenario: A fake satisfies the port
  Given a class with chat(agent_name, messages) -> str

  Then pyright reports no error

docs.text: Agents have no way to call a model today. This task adds the one shared client for an OpenAI-compatible server. It serves the Business Goals, Failure Modes and Success Metrics of requirements.md.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
Path 2 of decision.md. In src/core/llm/client.py: - class LLMClient is the only public name. __init__(self, settings: Settings, *, transport: httpx.BaseTransport | None = None). chat(self, agent_name: str, messages: list[dict[str, str]]) -> str. It satisfies ChatModel. - chat order: empty messages raises ValueError. Then resolve(settings, agent_name) (raises LLMConfigError for an unknown agent, no model or a bad URL). No request is sent before these pass. - Request: POST {base_url.rstrip("/")}/chat/completions, JSON body {"model": model, "messages": messages}. Header Authorization: Bearer <key> only when the key is not empty. - Follow the Mistral OCR adapter (src/agents/fetch/ocr/mistral.py): follow_redirects=False, trust_env=False, injectable transport, no logging. - Pass httpx.Timeout(timeout / 4) to the request. Stream the body. Cap it at 1 MiB (1048576 bytes). Use a monotonic deadline checked before each read and after each chunk. - Error mapping: - Deadline or httpx timeout: LLMTimeoutError, within 1.25 × timeout + 1 s. Each httpx phase gets timeout / 4. - Body over 1 MiB: LLMError. - Status not 2xx: LLMError with status_code. - Other httpx transport error: LLMError with status_code=None. - Non-JSON body, no choices, or non-string choices[0].message.content: LLMError with status_code=200. - Error text holds no API key, no message content and no base URL. - Answer: choices[0].message.content.

Tests in tests/unit/core/llm/test_client.py use httpx.MockTransport. The timeout test uses 0.2 s and checks elapsed time under 1.25 s. A second test stalls after one chunk (read timeout from request.extensions["timeout"]["read"]) and checks the same bound and that the read timeout is timeout / 4. Coverage of src/core/llm/ is 100 %.

Decided (default kept): Exact error message texts are not in decision.md. Tests assert type, status_code and absence of secrets, not full text. Decided (default kept): A body that is invalid JSON with a non-2xx status: status error wins (default in this spec).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The online Alembic run takes pg_advisory_lock on key 0x6C61775F6D6967 with no time limit. The DBA review and the security review of the run-once change rated this medium. Requirements are in requirements.md. Size S, so two lenses were compared.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Path 1: keep the poll loop in migrations/env.py. Effort S. Only subprocess tests reach the loop.
  • Path 2: move the lock into src/storage/advisory_lock.py with an injectable clock and sleep. Effort S-M. Unit tests reach the loop without a database.
Row Path 1 Path 2 Fit to constraints All met All met Failure modes All listed, holder race only as "unknown" All listed, each one unit-tested Complexity Low, one file Low, one new module Effort S S-M Main risk Coverage and mutation gates do not see the loop Wrong pg_locks key split

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Path 2, chosen by the owner on 2026-11-17. - The coverage and mutation gates of CONTRIBUTING.md can measure the lock logic. - Fake clock and sleep make the 1 s poll and the deadline testable without delays. - env.py stays a thin Alembic entry point.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The diff is larger than Path 1: the module has about 115 lines, plus tests.
  • migrations/env.py imports storage.advisory_lock.
  • The integration test must assert the real holder pid to guard the classid/objid split.
  • docs/migrations.md, section "Overlapping upgrade runs", describes the deadline, the setting and the error.

docs.title: Business Goals
docs.text:
• An operator who runs alembic upgrade head gets a clear failure within a known time when another session holds the migration lock. Today the run waits with no limit.
  • This closes the medium finding of the DBA review and the security review of the run-once change: a hung run, or any role that takes the key 0x6C61775F6D6967, blocks every later upgrade.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL session advisory lock, key 0x6C61775F6D6967, taken in migrations/env.py (online mode only).
  • The run polls pg_try_advisory_lock every 1 s until the deadline. It does not use pg_advisory_lock with lock_timeout.
  • The deadline is a typed property in src/config/settings.py, read from the environment variable MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S. Default: 300 s.
  • The value must be a positive number. A non-numeric or non-positive value fails at start with an error that names the variable.
  • No new dependency. Python 3.13, SQLAlchemy, Alembic.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• The lock is free: the first try succeeds, the run logs no wait line, and migrations run as today.
  • The lock is held and is freed before the deadline: the run takes the lock at the next poll and applies only the missing revisions.
  • The lock is held past the deadline: the run fails. It applies no revision, and alembic_version is unchanged.
  • The holder ended between the last try and the pg_locks query: the error says the holder is unknown.
  • MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S is 0, -5 or abc: the run fails before it connects.
  • Offline mode (--sql) takes no lock and reads no deadline.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• On timeout the run raises an error (a RuntimeError subclass). The message names the key 0x6C61775F6D6967, the deadline in seconds, and the holder backend pid from pg_locks, or "unknown".
  • The process exits non-zero, so the one-shot init service fails and dependent services do not start.
  • When the first try fails, the run logs one line: it waits for the key, with the deadline.
  • A failed poll query (connection lost) raises the database error. It is not reported as a timeout.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
• An integration test holds the key on a second connection, sets the deadline to 2 s, and checks that the run fails in 2 s to 5 s with the key and the holder pid in the message.
  • The same test checks that alembic_version has 0 changed rows.
  • 3 of the 4 existing tests in tests/integration/test_migration_lock.py pass unchanged. test_upgrade_blocks_while_lock_held detects the wait from the wait log line or a still-running process, because polling leaves no not-granted row in pg_locks.
  • Unit tests cover the setting: default 300, valid value, and 3 invalid values (0, -5, abc).
  • Quality gate: ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright and pytest all pass. Coverage and mutation gates of CONTRIBUTING.md pass.

docs.title: Path 1: single-file change
docs.text:
• The poll loop, MigrationLockTimeout(RuntimeError) and _lock_holder_pid stay in migrations/env.py.
  • Settings.migration_lock_timeout_s reuses _positive("MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S", "300", float).
  • run_migrations_online reads the deadline before connect(). Offline mode does not read it.
  • Holder pid: pg_locks with locktype='advisory', granted, classid = high 32 bits, objid = low 32 bits, objsubid=1.
  • The try/finally release starts after the loop, so a timeout never calls pg_advisory_unlock.
  • Tests: subprocess integration tests only, because env.py runs migrations on import.
  • Effort: S, about 30 lines.
  • Main risk: coverage and mutation gates do not measure subprocess runs.

docs.title: Path 2: extracted lock module
docs.text:
• New module src/storage/advisory_lock.py: context manager advisory_lock(connection, key, timeout_s, *, clock=time.monotonic, sleep=time.sleep, poll_s=1.0).
  • AdvisoryLockTimeout(RuntimeError) with key, timeout_s, holder_pid: int | None. The message names the key in hex, the deadline, and the pid or "unknown".
  • Loop: try pg_try_advisory_lock, end the transaction after each try, log one wait line on the first failure, sleep poll_s, stop at the deadline.
  • On the deadline: query the holder in pg_locks (key split into classid/objid, objsubid=1), then raise. The body never runs.
  • A database error in a poll or in the pg_locks query propagates unchanged.
  • Release keeps the current behaviour: log a failure, do not raise.
  • Settings.migration_lock_timeout_s reuses _positive("MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S", "300", float).
  • migrations/env.py keeps MIGRATION_LOCK_KEY, reads the deadline before connect(), and calls the module.
  • Tests: unit tests with a fake connection, clock and sleep. One subprocess integration test with a held key.
  • Effort: S-M, about 80 lines.
  • Main risk: a wrong classid/objid split gives "unknown". The integration test asserts the real pid.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The lock logic moves into a testable module with an injectable clock and sleep. It polls with a deadline and reports the holder. It serves the requirements for the poll, the timeout error and the unit-test success metric.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
• Create src/storage/advisory_lock.py with context manager advisory_lock(connection, key, timeout_s, *, clock=time.monotonic, sleep=time.sleep, poll_s=1.0).
  • Define AdvisoryLockTimeout(RuntimeError) with key, timeout_s, holder_pid: int | None. The message has the key in hex, the deadline, and the pid or "unknown".
  • Loop: run pg_try_advisory_lock, end the transaction after each try, log one wait line on the first failure, sleep poll_s, stop at the deadline.
  • On the deadline, query pg_locks with the key split into classid/objid and objsubid=1. Then raise. The body never runs.
  • A database error in a poll or in the pg_locks query propagates unchanged.
  • Release logs a failure and does not raise.
  • Tests in tests/unit/test_advisory_lock.py use a fake connection, clock and sleep.
  • Resolved: use stdlib logging.getLogger(__name__), as plugins/relational_db/postgres.py does.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Scenario: free lock Given the first try returns true When the context is entered Then the body runs And no wait line is logged And sleep is never called

Scenario: lock freed before the deadline Given the first try returns false and the second returns true When the context is entered Then sleep is called once with 1.0 And exactly one wait line is logged And the body runs

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The one-shot init service already runs alembic upgrade head before the app and the worker start, and the stores only check the schema head. Two upgrade runs can still overlap: an operator by hand, a second stack, or the test service. Overlapping runs fail with "already exists" errors.

The issue asks for a test that starts two stores on an empty database. That test no longer applies, because PostgreSQLStore.initialize() does not migrate. It only checks the head and raises SchemaNotAtHeadError. The acceptance evidence is test_concurrent_upgrades_apply_once: two alembic upgrade head runs on an empty database, and both reach head.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Path 1: a session-level pg_advisory_lock in migrations/env.py, on the same connection as the DDL. It covers every caller.
  • Path 2: a bootstrap.migrate wrapper with the lock on a second connection. It changes init, and the plain alembic CLI skips the lock.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Path 1. The architect and the DBA both found it feasible and recommended it. Both rejected path 2. - Lock key: a fixed literal bigint constant 0x6C61775F6D6967 ("law_mig"). Do not compute the key with hashtext(). The tests copy the literal, because an import of env.py runs the migrations. The blocking test fails if the two keys differ. - Order: take the lock, commit to end the autobegin transaction, then context.configure and begin_transaction / run_migrations. - finally: roll back an open transaction, then unlock and commit. A try/except logs an unlock error, so it cannot hide the original error. NullPool closes the session, which frees the lock anyway. - Use a session lock, never pg_advisory_xact_lock. - Offline mode takes no lock.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One file of product code changes. init, the stores and the schema stay as they are.
  • migrations/ is outside coverage and mutation scope. Four Docker integration tests are the proof: concurrent runs, deterministic blocking, a failed upgrade that frees the key, and offline mode with the key held.
  • A run waits with no limit while another run holds the lock. A future lock_timeout would make the waiting run fail.

docs.title: Review warnings kept
docs.text:
• No lock timeout (perf and security, medium). The requirements accept an unlimited wait. Any role can take the key, but that needs SQL access to the database first. A deadline with pg_try_advisory_lock is a possible follow-up.
  • No test proves that the finally unlock runs. A subprocess frees the lock when it exits, so a test cannot see the difference. The failed-upgrade test proves that the error is not hidden and that the key is free afterwards. For the same reason, the "no lock left at head" test was dropped.
  • The test copies the lock key (style). An import of env.py runs the migrations. The blocking test fails if the keys differ.
  • The offline test runs only to the first revision. A later migration reads data, which --sql mode cannot do (this was true before this change).
  • Style items 3, 6 and 7 (repeated key dict, "Scenario:" docstrings, inline unlock in the tests) stay as they are. They are small and readable.

docs.title: Business Goals
docs.text:
• The one-shot init service already runs alembic upgrade head before the app and the worker start. Stores only check the schema head.
  • A second alembic upgrade head can still start at the same time: an operator by hand, a second stack on the same database, or the test service next to init.
  • Goal: concurrent upgrade runs apply each migration once. No run crashes with "already exists" errors.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• Python 3.13, Alembic, SQLAlchemy 2.x, PostgreSQL. The lock lives in migrations/env.py, online mode only.
  • The owner role lawbyai_owner runs migrations. It can call pg_advisory_lock (no extra grant needed).
  • No new migration, no schema change, no new dependency. No change to init or to the stores.
  • Offline mode (--sql) has no connection and takes no lock.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• Empty database: the first run creates alembic_version. The second run waits, then sees head and does nothing.
  • Database already at head: the run takes the lock, does nothing, and releases the lock.
  • A third concurrent run: it waits like the second one.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• A migration fails: the run rolls back its transaction, releases the lock and re-raises. The waiting run then takes the lock and tries again from the same revision.
  • A process dies while it holds the lock: PostgreSQL ends the session and frees the session-level lock.
  • A run waits with no time limit while another run holds the lock. This is accepted: migrations are short, and a hung run is visible in pg_locks.
  • If a role or the server later sets lock_timeout or statement_timeout, the waiting run fails with a timeout error. No timeout is set today.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
• 2 concurrent alembic upgrade head processes on an empty scratch database: both exit 0, and alembic_version holds exactly 1 row equal to head. 1 integration test.
  • While one session holds the lock key, a second alembic upgrade head is still running after 2 s and exits 0 after the lock is released: 1 integration test.
  • A run on a database at head exits 0 and leaves no advisory lock in pg_locks: 1 integration test.
  • Gate: ruff, ruff format, pyright, fast tests, Docker suite, CI mutation gate. 0 failures.

docs.title: Path 1: in-process lock in the migration environment
docs.text:
• Only run_migrations_online() in migrations/env.py changes. Offline mode, init, the stores and the schema stay as they are.
  • A module constant _MIGRATION_LOCK_KEY (a fixed bigint) and a context manager _advisory_lock(connection).
  • Order: open the connection (NullPool), run SELECT pg_advisory_lock(:key), commit to end the autobegin transaction, then context.configure and begin_transaction / run_migrations inside try.
  • finally: roll back an open transaction, run pg_advisory_unlock, commit.
  • Session-level lock on the same connection as the DDL, so one session holds it for the whole run. A waiting run reads alembic_version only after it holds the lock, sees head and does nothing.
  • Failures: a failed migration rolls back, unlocks and re-raises. A dead process frees the lock with its session. No lock timeout (accepted).
  • Tests: two concurrent alembic upgrade head subprocesses on an empty scratch database (both exit 0, 1 row at head); one run at head leaves no advisory lock in pg_locks.
  • Risks: transaction order with the pinned Alembic version; the race test can pass by luck without the lock; pyright typing.
  • Effort: S. About 20 lines in one file plus 2 integration tests. Covers every caller: init, the operator CLI, the test service.

docs.title: Path 2: single migration entry point outside Alembic
docs.text:
• New src/bootstrap/migrate.py with upgrade_locked(url) and main() for python -m bootstrap.migrate.
  • It opens a separate AUTOCOMMIT NullPool connection, takes pg_advisory_lock, calls alembic.command.upgrade(cfg, "head"), and unlocks and closes in finally.
  • docker/docker-compose.yml init and test commands and init_stack.alembic_upgrade call it. migrations/env.py stays as it is.
  • Failures: same as path 1. Closing the lock connection frees the lock even if the unlock fails.
  • Tests: two concurrent python -m bootstrap.migrate subprocesses on an empty scratch database; one run at head leaves no lock. Unit test for the unlock order with a fake connection.
  • Risks: the plain alembic upgrade head CLI skips the lock (operator runs, the hint in schema_check.py). Two connections: if the lock connection drops, the lock is lost during the migration. It conflicts with requirements.md (no change to init).
  • Effort: S, but compose edits need a Docker suite run.
