docs.text:
• Path 1: reviewed YAML files in the repo, loaded into memory. No database. Effort S.
  • Path 2: shared PostgreSQL tables, filled by a seed script. Effort M.
  • Path 2, extended (chosen): path 2 plus one import function for runtime uploads and an append-only revision table.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Path 2, extended. The owner chose the database and a YAML upload by the admin UI. The UI page is a follow-up issue.

docs.title: Module
docs.text:
Layering follows src/core/users/ and ADR-0014. core/procedures/ holds no SQL. The SQL adapter is a direct integration beside PostgreSQLStore. It is not a method of that class, because procedures are a separate aggregate and the class is already large.

In src/core/procedures/ (imports only core.security and its own modules): - models.py: frozen pydantic Step and Procedure with extra="forbid". - Step: key (stable id inside the procedure, kebab-case), text, source_url (https, no credentials), last_checked (a date, not in the future), verify_with_office (non-empty). - Procedure: schema_version, slug, title, steps (at least 1, unique key, sorted by position), revision (set by the repository on read, not part of the YAML). - ProcedureSummary: slug, title. - ImportResult: slug, revision, changed: bool. - errors.py: ProcedureValidationError(source, step_key, reason) and ProcedureStoreError. - parse.py: parse_procedure_yaml(text, today) -> Procedure. The clock is a parameter. - ports.py: the ProcedureRepository Protocol (save(procedure, actor) -> ImportResult, get(slug), list()). - service.py: ProcedureService(repository). - import_procedure(text) -> ImportResult. It calls require_admin_principal() first, before any session opens, and takes the actor from the principal. It parses, then calls repository.save. - get_procedure(slug) -> Procedure | None. None means not found. A malformed slug also returns None. - list_procedures() -> list[ProcedureSummary], sorted by slug. - Errors: ProcedureValidationError for bad input, PrincipalRequiredError for a non-admin, ProcedureStoreError for a database failure (the cause is chained, and the message holds no content).

In src/plugins/relational_db/procedures.py: PostgresProcedureRepository(engine). Each call opens its own session. Reads return frozen pydantic objects, so no lazy load happens after the session closes. A UNIQUE(procedure_id, revision) IntegrityError maps to ProcedureStoreError. The ORM tables sit in src/data/models.py, next to Base.

Citation rule for the bureaucracy assistant: a curated step has no confidence score. The assistant cites a step by slug, key and revision, with its source_url and last_checked. It is not a retrieved chunk.

Identical content: compare procedure.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"revision"}) with the content of the latest revision (jsonb equality). The actor does not count. If equal, write nothing and return changed=False. The first import is revision 1.

Seed actor: the seed runs inside principal_context(RequestPrincipal(email="system:seed", role=ADMIN)).

docs.title: Data
docs.text: One Alembic migration after head c4a91e7f2b58. Every column is NOT NULL. The migration sets SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s' in upgrade and downgrade. The downgrade stops when procedure_revision holds rows. Names are frozen literals. Server: PostgreSQL 18. - procedure: id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY, slug unique, title, schema_version, revision, updated_at timestamptz default now(). CHECKs: slug ~ '^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$', btrim(title) <> '', revision >= 1, schema_version >= 1. - procedure_step: PK (procedure_id, position). procedure_id FK ON DELETE CASCADE, key, text, source_url, last_checked DATE, verify_with_office. UNIQUE(procedure_id, key). CHECKs: position >= 0, key kebab-case, non-empty text and verify line, source_url LIKE 'https://%'. - procedure_revision: append-only. id identity, procedure_id FK ON DELETE RESTRICT (a cascade would bypass the append-only rule), revision >= 1, content JSONB with CHECK jsonb_typeof(content) = 'object', actor (non-empty), created_at timestamptz default now(). UNIQUE(procedure_id, revision). - content is Procedure.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"revision"}). It is the only full history, because steps are replaced. - No tenant_id and no RLS (shared reference data). - Grants to lawbyai_app, explicit, TRUNCATE revoked: - procedure: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE. No DELETE, because no import deletes a procedure. - procedure_step: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE. - procedure_revision: SELECT, INSERT. - The ORM tables are in src/data/models.py on the same Base that migrations/env.py reads, so autogenerate sees them.

docs.title: Import order
docs.text:
One READ COMMITTED transaction, in this order: 1. INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (slug) DO UPDATE SET slug = EXCLUDED.slug RETURNING id, revision. This locks the row, also for a new slug. 2. Compare the new content with the latest revision row (jsonb equality). If equal, roll back and return "unchanged". Do not touch updated_at. 3. Delete the steps of the procedure and insert the new steps. 4. UPDATE procedure SET revision = revision + 1, then insert the revision row.

Reads: get_procedure reads the procedure and its steps in one statement (join), so a reader never mixes an old title with new steps.

docs.title: Seed
docs.text: scripts/seed_db.py reads data/procedures/*.yaml (3 files: PESEL, residence card, tax ID). It runs as lawbyai_app (POSTGRES_URL) inside principal_context(RequestPrincipal("system:seed", ADMIN)) and calls import_procedure. Git keeps the history of the seed content. The revision table keeps the history of runtime changes. The seed is idempotent. Run order: migrate, then seed. docs/migrations.md states it.

docs.title: Follow-up issues
docs.text:
• Admin upload page in Streamlit (calls ProcedureService.import_procedure).
  • Draft and approval state for uploaded procedures (OPEN: today an admin upload is live at once).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Many procedures and runtime upload are possible, with one rule set (pydantic) and the DB constraints as a second guard.
  • History is kept twice: Git for the seed files and revision rows for runtime edits.
  • Known limit: writes are guarded by RBAC in code only. Any app code path, including the Celery worker, can write. Every write leaves a revision row. The strategic fix is a follow-up: a SECURITY DEFINER import function, with the app limited to SELECT and EXECUTE (as public.auth_lookup_user).
  • Cost: a migration, a seed step in deploy, and drift if the seed is not rerun. A rerun is safe because the seed is idempotent.
  • The issue text changes: it drops "seed in scripts/seed_db.py (exists)", sets the new files, and gets a Contract section for the bureaucracy assistant.

docs.title: Requirements: procedure-kb
docs.text: Source: the issue "Bureaucracy knowledge base: schema and 3 seed procedures". Facts come from pyproject.toml, src/data/, docs/adr/0008-mvp-scope.md, docs/adr/0015-information-only-answers.md and the issue "Bureaucracy assistant agent" (the consumer).

docs.title: Business Goals
docs.text:
• The bureaucracy assistant needs checked procedure data. A wrong step can harm a user (a missed deadline, a wrong office). Today no procedure data exists.
  • Each step carries its source and the date a person last checked it. The user sees where a step comes from and how old it is.
  • Three procedures ship first: PESEL, residence card, tax ID. The owner reviews every source and step before merge. A lawyer reviews before v1.
  • Decided (owner, G1, 2026-11-27): there will be many procedures, and admins will add them at runtime by uploading YAML. So the data lives in the database, with a revision history. The upload page is a follow-up issue. This task delivers the module under it.
  • Decided: the consumer is the bureaucracy assistant. It needs "find a procedure by slug" and a list call for a menu.
  • Non-goals: the upload page (follow-up issue), auto-update of steps, more than the 3 seed procedures, a draft or approval state for uploads (OPEN, follow-up).

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• Python 3.13. pydantic==2.14.2 and pyyaml==6.0.3 are already dependencies. No new dependency.
  • A separate module src/core/procedures/ (pydantic models, YAML parser, import service, read calls). Seed content in data/procedures/*.yaml, loaded by scripts/seed_db.py (new). Tests in tests/unit/ and tests/integration/.
  • One import function takes YAML text and an actor, validates it, and writes it to the database. The seed script and the later upload page both call it.
  • Tables procedure, procedure_step and procedure_revision (append-only), one Alembic migration. The tables are shared, with no tenant_id and no RLS. Writes need the admin principal.
  • Step fields: text, source_url, last_checked (a date), and the line "verify with the office". A step with an empty source_url, an invalid date or no verify line fails validation.
  • Exactly 3 seed procedures: PESEL, residence card, tax ID.
  • Unit tests use no network. The source_url value is validated as an https URL by syntax only.
  • Budget: 4-6 GB host. The data is small (3 files). The loader adds no service and no background thread.
  • Wording follows ADR-0015: information, not advice. Only lawful procedures.
  • scripts/seed_db.py is named by the issue but does not exist (checked 2026-11-27). This task creates it.
  • The "date not in the future" rule lives in pydantic only (a SQL CHECK with CURRENT_DATE is not immutable). The clock is injectable for tests.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• A YAML file with an empty source_url, a missing last_checked, a date in the future, or no verify line: the import raises an error that names the file (or the upload) and the step. Nothing is written.
  • A malformed YAML file or one with an unknown key: loading raises an error that names the file.
  • Two seed files with the same slug: the seed stops and names both files. Importing a slug that exists adds a new revision and replaces the steps in one transaction.
  • An import by a caller that is not an admin: PrincipalRequiredError. Nothing is written.
  • An import of identical content: no new revision.
  • Unknown slug: the find call returns a clear "not found" result. It does not raise a bare KeyError.
  • An empty table: the list call returns an empty list.
  • A procedure with zero steps fails validation.
  • A source_url with a scheme other than https, or with credentials: validation fails.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Bad data must never reach the assistant. The import validates before any write and runs in one transaction: a failure leaves the old data.
  • History must survive. The app role cannot change or delete a revision row.
  • A stale last_checked date is shown to the user. The system does not hide it. Auto-update is a non-goal.
  • The owner gate is a process rule: an approving PR review from the owner before merge. A test cannot prove it. The PR text states it.
  • A change to the step schema must not break the assistant silently. The schema has a version field and a test that pins the fields.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
• 4 of 4 Gherkin scenarios of the issue pass: seed has exactly 3 procedures, every step is complete, bad data is rejected, the owner gate holds.
  • 3 of 3 seed procedures import with 0 validation errors, and a second seed run adds no revision.
  • Each import writes one revision row with the actor and the time. The app role cannot UPDATE or DELETE a revision row (privilege test).
  • 3 of 3 seed procedures have at least 3 steps and every step has a source link.
  • Line coverage of src/core/procedures/ is 100 % in unit tests. Diff coverage meets the CONTRIBUTING.md gate.
  • Quality gate: ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright, pytest all pass with 0 errors.
  • get_procedure and list_procedures return in under 100 ms for the 3 seed procedures (integration test).

docs.title: Review: procedure-kb
docs.text: Verdict: PASS WITH WARNINGS (2026-11-27). Scope: main..HEAD, 14 commits.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text:
• Gate: ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright, bandit and unit tests pass (run by the main session with the main checkout venv, because the gate agent could not run tools in the worktree). Not run locally: pip-audit, mutation score, diff-cover (CI runs them).
  • TDD order check: pass, no violation in the range.
  • Database tests: run on a disposable PostgreSQL 18.6 with the project role script. Procedure files: 43 passed. Whole integration suite: 271 passed, 9 skipped (no Valkey, no live Sejm), 2 failed in test_login_flow.py (cookie fake of the login UI, no shared code with this change, to be confirmed on CI).
  • Structure, security, style, performance: no critical or high finding.

docs.title: Findings fixed in this change
docs.text: YAML size cap and duplicate-key check, strict source_url characters and length, attacker text kept out of error messages, get wraps a bad stored row in ProcedureStoreError, lock_timeout on save, seed script handles unreadable files and uses one clock, tri-state compare made explicit, duplicate sort removed, task ids removed from code.

docs.title: Findings kept as follow-ups
docs.text:
• source_url host allowlist (an owner decision: allowed domains).
  • Rename the port method list (shadows the builtin).
  • Step count and upload size limits belong to the upload page.
  • QA-080: seed against a stopped server shows no password (no test yet).
  • Writes are guarded in code only. The strategic fix is a SECURITY DEFINER import function.
  • A draft or approval state for uploaded procedures.

docs.title: Path 1: file-based, read-only content
docs.text: Lens: procedures are reviewed YAML files in the repo. No database table and no seed script.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• data/procedures/{pesel,residence-card,tax-id}.yaml: one procedure per file. The slug field names the procedure. The file name is not trusted.
  • src/data/procedures.py: frozen pydantic models and the loader.
  • Step (extra="forbid"): text, source_url (https only, no credentials), last_checked (a date, not in the future), verify_with_office (non-empty line).
  • Procedure (extra="forbid"): schema_version (Literal[1]), slug, title, steps (at least 1).
  • ProcedureLoadError(file, step_index, reason).
  • tests/unit/test_procedures_schema.py.

docs.title: Interfaces
docs.text:
• load_procedures(directory: Path = DEFAULT_DIR) -> dict[str, Procedure]. Raises ProcedureLoadError.
  • list_procedures() -> list[Procedure], sorted by slug, [] for an empty directory.
  • get_procedure(slug: str) -> Procedure | None. None means not found.
  • The two public calls use a lazy cache over the default directory.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text: First call loads each *.yaml in sorted order with yaml.safe_load, validates it, wraps ValidationError and YAMLError into ProcedureLoadError, checks duplicate slugs, and caches an immutable registry.

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text: Fail closed: one invalid file stops the load and names the file. Schema drift is pinned by schema_version and a field-pin test. The owner gate is a PR rule. A bad file on main fails on first use, so a CI test over the real data/procedures/ directory gates merge.

docs.title: Effort and risk
docs.text: Effort S. Risks: one bad file takes all procedures down (guard: the CI test), content updates need a deploy, and the issue text names scripts/seed_db.py, so the issue must be amended.

docs.title: Path 2: database-backed, seeded
docs.text: Lens: procedures and steps are shared PostgreSQL tables filled by a seed script from the same YAML files.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• data/procedures/*.yaml and the pydantic models and load_procedures in src/data/procedures.py (as in path 1).
  • scripts/seed_db.py (new, absent today): load, validate, upsert in one transaction.
  • Alembic migration after head c4a91e7f2b58: tables procedure and procedure_step, CHECK constraints (https URL, non-empty verify line, date not in the future), UNIQUE(slug), UNIQUE(procedure_id, position).
  • ORM models, for example src/plugins/relational_db/procedure_models.py.
  • PostgreSQLStore.get_procedure(slug) and list_procedures().

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text: An operator runs the migration and then the seed. The seed stops before any write if a file is invalid. It upserts by slug, replaces steps and deletes procedures that left the files. The assistant reads through the store with plain SELECTs. The app role gets SELECT only.

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text: Two gates: pydantic at seed and DB constraints. A failed seed rolls back. Not handled: direct SQL edits by a privileged role, and drift when nobody reruns the seed (needs a deploy step or a startup check). "At least one step" needs a deferred constraint trigger.

docs.title: Effort and risk
docs.text: Effort M. Risks: a DB and a seed deploy step for 3 files of data, drift between files and rows, and SQL CHECKs that can disagree with the pydantic rules.

docs.title: T1: Procedure models, errors and YAML parser (pure)
Context
docs.text: The bureaucracy assistant needs checked procedure data. A bad step can harm a user. This task builds the pure layer: models, errors and the parser. It serves the step-field, validation and schema-version rules in requirements.md.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text: Create src/core/procedures/ with these files. The package imports only core.security and its own modules. It holds no SQL. - models.py: frozen pydantic models with extra="forbid". - Step: key (kebab-case), text, source_url (https only, no credentials, syntax check only), last_checked (date, not in the future), verify_with_office (non-empty). - Procedure: schema_version, slug, title, steps (at least 1, unique key, sorted by position), revision (set by the repository on read, not in the YAML). - ProcedureSummary: slug, title. ImportResult: slug, revision, changed: bool. - errors.py: ProcedureValidationError(source, step_key, reason) and ProcedureStoreError. Messages hold no content. - parse.py: parse_procedure_yaml(text, today) -> Procedure. Use yaml.safe_load. The clock is a parameter. Wrap YAML errors and pydantic errors into ProcedureValidationError that names the source and the step key. - __init__.py: export the public names. - Tests in tests/unit/core/procedures/test_models_parse.py. No network.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Scenario: valid procedure parses Given a YAML text with 3 complete steps and a past last_checked When parse_procedure_yaml(text, today) runs Then it returns a Procedure with 3 steps in position order

Scenario: incomplete step is rejected Given a step with an empty source_url, or a missing last_checked, or no verify_with_office When the text is parsed Then ProcedureValidationError is raised and its step_key names that step

Scenario: future or invalid date is rejected Given a step with last_checked after today, or "not-a-date" When the text is parsed Then ProcedureValidationError is raised

Scenario: bad URL is rejected Given a source_url with http:// or with user:pw@ credentials When the text is parsed Then ProcedureValidationError is raised

Scenario: structure errors are rejected Given a procedure with zero steps, an unknown key, duplicate step keys, or malformed YAML When the text is parsed Then ProcedureValidationError is raised and its source is set

Scenario: schema is pinned Given the Step model and schema_version When the test reads Step.model_fields keys Then they equal exactly key, text, source_url, last_checked, verify_with_office, and the test pins the schema_version value

docs.title: T2: Repository port and ProcedureService with fake repository
Context
docs.text: The service is the one entry point for the seed script, the later upload page and the assistant. It enforces the admin rule before any database work. It serves the admin-write, identical-content and not-found rules in requirements.md.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text: Add to src/core/procedures/ (imports only core.security and its own modules, no SQL): - ports.py: ProcedureRepository Protocol with save(procedure, actor) -> ImportResult, get(slug) -> Procedure | None, list() -> list[ProcedureSummary]. - service.py: ProcedureService(repository). - import_procedure(text) -> ImportResult: call require_admin_principal() first, before any session opens. Take the actor from the principal. Parse with parse_procedure_yaml, then call repository.save. - get_procedure(slug) -> Procedure | None: None for not found and for a malformed slug (check the slug pattern before the repository call). - list_procedures() -> list[ProcedureSummary], sorted by slug. - Errors: ProcedureValidationError for bad input, PrincipalRequiredError for a non-admin, ProcedureStoreError for a store failure. Chain the cause. The message holds no content. - Tests in tests/unit/core/procedures/test_procedure_service.py use an in-memory fake repository that follows the port. - Checked: require_admin_principal, RequestPrincipal and principal_context exist in core/security/principal.py. Import them from there if core.security does not export them.

Scenario: admin import Given an admin principal with email "a@x.org" and valid YAML When import_procedure(text) runs Then save is called once with actor "a@x.org" and the result is returned

docs.title: T3: ORM tables, Alembic migration, grants and privilege tests
Context
docs.text: Procedures live in shared PostgreSQL tables with an append-only revision history. The database constraints are a second guard after pydantic. This task serves the table, history and grant rules in requirements.md.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
• src/data/models.py: add ORM tables procedure, procedure_step, procedure_revision on the same Base that migrations/env.py reads. No tenant_id, no RLS. Every column NOT NULL.
  • migrations/versions/procedure_kb_tables.py: one migration after head c4a91e7f2b58. Use frozen literal names. Run SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s' in upgrade and downgrade. The downgrade stops with an error when procedure_revision holds rows.
  • procedure: id BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY, slug unique, title, schema_version, revision, updated_at timestamptz default now(). CHECKs: slug ~ '^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$', btrim(title) <> '', revision >= 1, schema_version >= 1.
  • procedure_step: PK (procedure_id, position). procedure_id FK ON DELETE CASCADE, key, text, source_url, last_checked DATE, verify_with_office. UNIQUE(procedure_id, key). CHECKs: position >= 0, key kebab-case, non-empty text and verify line, source_url LIKE 'https://%'.
  • procedure_revision: id identity, procedure_id FK ON DELETE RESTRICT, revision >= 1, content JSONB with CHECK jsonb_typeof(content) = 'object', actor non-empty, created_at timestamptz default now(), UNIQUE(procedure_id, revision).
  • Grants to lawbyai_app, explicit, TRUNCATE revoked: procedure SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE. procedure_step SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE. procedure_revision SELECT, INSERT.
  • Tests in tests/integration/test_procedure_schema.py. Run them in the Docker suite on PostgreSQL 18. Connect as the owner role for the DDL and CHECK tests, and as lawbyai_app for the privilege tests.
  • The "date not in the future" rule stays in pydantic only.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Scenario: migration round trip Given a database at head c4a91e7f2b58 When alembic upgrade head then alembic downgrade -1 run with no revision rows Then the three tables exist after upgrade and none exist after downgrade

Scenario: CHECK constraints reject bad rows Given the migrated schema When a test inserts a bad slug, an empty title, revision 0, source_url "http://x", an empty step text, a non-object content, or an empty actor Then each insert fails with a check violation

Scenario: app role cannot change history Given a connection as lawbyai_app and one revision row When it runs UPDATE or DELETE on procedure_revision, DELETE on procedure, or TRUNCATE on any of the three tables Then each statement fails with permission denied

Scenario: app role can do its writes Given a connection as lawbyai_app When it inserts and updates procedure, and inserts, updates and deletes procedure_step, and inserts procedure_revision Then each statement succeeds

Scenario: revision rows block procedure delete Given a procedure with a revision row When the owner role deletes the procedure Then the delete fails with a foreign key violation

Scenario: downgrade guards history Given procedure_revision holds one row When alembic downgrade -1 runs Then it stops with an error and the tables remain

docs.title: T4: PostgresProcedureRepository with concurrency and read tests
Context
docs.text: The SQL adapter implements the ProcedureRepository port against the T3 tables. It keeps an import atomic and keeps history. It serves the transaction, identical-content and revision rules in requirements.md.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
In src/plugins/relational_db/procedures.py add PostgresProcedureRepository(engine). It sits beside PostgreSQLStore and is not a method of it. Each call opens its own session. Reads return frozen pydantic objects, so no lazy load happens after the session closes.

save(procedure, actor) runs in one READ COMMITTED transaction, in this order: 1. INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (slug) DO UPDATE SET slug = EXCLUDED.slug RETURNING id, revision. This locks the row, also for a new slug. 2. Compare procedure.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"revision"}) with the content of the latest revision (jsonb equality). The actor does not count. If equal, roll back, return changed=False, and do not touch updated_at. 3. Delete the steps of the procedure and insert the new steps. 4. UPDATE procedure SET revision = revision + 1, then insert the revision row with the actor. The first import is revision 1.

get(slug) reads the procedure and its steps in one join statement. list() returns summaries sorted by slug. A UNIQUE(procedure_id, revision) IntegrityError and other database errors map to ProcedureStoreError with the cause chained and no content in the message.

Tests in tests/integration/test_procedure_repository.py run in the Docker suite and connect as lawbyai_app.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Scenario: first save Given an empty database When save runs for slug "pesel" Then the result is revision 1 with changed=True and one revision row exists with the actor

Scenario: identical content Given "pesel" is saved When save runs again with equal content and another actor Then changed=False, the revision count is unchanged and updated_at is unchanged

Scenario: changed content Given "pesel" is saved at revision 1 When save runs with one step text changed Then the result is revision 2 and get("pesel") returns the new steps only

Scenario: failed save keeps old data Given "pesel" is saved When a save fails in the middle, for example a step violates a CHECK Then ProcedureStoreError is raised and get("pesel") returns the old data at the old revision

Scenario: concurrent saves Given "pesel" exists When two threads save different content for it at the same time Then the revisions are distinct and consecutive, and the revision rows match the final state

Scenario: not found and empty Given an empty database When get("nope") and list() run Then get returns None and list returns an empty list

Scenario: read speed Given 3 saved procedures When get and list run Then each returns in under 100 ms

docs.text:

  • The quality gate reports pass or skipped (never fail).
  • No OPEN: item remains.

docs.title: Build notes (from T1)
docs.text:
• Procedure.model_dump(mode="json") holds revision. The identical-content compare and the stored content snapshot exclude revision (use model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"revision"})). parse_procedure_yaml rejects a revision key in YAML. The repository sets revision with model_copy(update=...) on read.
  • Rebuilding a stored step skips the future-date check (no clock context).
  • The first import inserts revision 1 (the CHECK needs revision >= 1). Each later import adds 1.

docs.title: T5: Three seed YAML files, seed script and run order doc
Context
docs.text: The assistant needs real procedures at first start. Three ship first: PESEL, residence card, tax ID. The owner reviews every source and step before merge. It serves the seed and idempotency rules in requirements.md.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
• data/procedures/pesel.yaml, residence-card.yaml, tax-id.yaml: each has schema_version, slug, title and at least 3 steps. Each step has key, text, source_url (https), last_checked and verify_with_office. Wording follows ADR-0015: information, not advice. Only lawful procedures.
  • scripts/seed_db.py (new): read data/procedures/*.yaml. Detect a duplicate slug before any write and stop with an error that names both files. Connect as lawbyai_app with POSTGRES_URL. Run inside principal_context(RequestPrincipal(email="system:seed", role=ADMIN)) and call ProcedureService.import_procedure for each file. Errors name the file. The seed is idempotent.
  • docs/migrations.md: state the run order, migrate then seed.
  • Tests: tests/unit/test_seed_procedures.py (no network, no database: parse all files, count, steps, duplicate slug using temp files) and tests/integration/test_seed_db.py (real database, Docker suite).
  • Content rule: the builder drafts each step only from an official source it has read (gov.pl, the Office for Foreigners, the tax office), through a research agent. Each source_url is a real page that was opened. last_checked is the date of that reading. The builder never fills a step from memory. The owner reviews every source and step in the PR.
  • Owner gate: an approving owner PR review before merge. It is a process rule and no test proves it. The PR text states it and says the drafts were prepared by an AI from official sources.

Scenario: exactly three seed files Given the directory data/procedures/ When the unit test lists *.yaml Then there are exactly 3 files with slugs "pesel", "residence-card" and "tax-id"

Scenario: seed content is complete Given the 3 seed files When each is parsed with parse_procedure_yaml Then there are 0 errors, each has at least 3 steps, and every step has an https source_url

Scenario: bad seed file Given a temp file with an empty source_url When the seed runs on that directory Then it fails naming the file and writes nothing

Scenario: duplicate slug Given two temp files with the same slug When the seed runs Then it stops before any write and the error names both files

Scenario: seed twice Given a migrated empty database When the seed runs two times as lawbyai_app Then there are 3 procedures, 3 revision rows after the first run, and the same 3 after the second

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The app role lawbyai_app can UPDATE and DELETE rows in rejected_document, so the audit log of admin rejects is mutable. PostgreSQLStore.reject takes the actor as a free admin argument, so a caller can write any email. No production code calls reject() yet. Only tests call it. The owner chose these rules: - Rows are kept forever. - Only the migration owner keeps the rights to change or delete rows. - The actor comes from the request context.

The owner delegated the G1 choice to the solution-architect and the DBA.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Path 1: a separate actor context variable (core.security.actor), which the caller sets around each reject call. It has no role check. Effort S.
  • Path 2: one request principal (tenant, email, role), which require_auth() sets on each rerun. The store checks the admin role. Effort M.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Path 2, reduced. The solution-architect picked it, and the DBA preferred it. The DBA's fixes F1 to F4 are added.

docs.title: Principal
docs.text:
• New module src/core/security/principal.py:
  • @dataclass(frozen=True) RequestPrincipal(email: str, role: str). It has no tenant_id, so it cannot drift from the tenant context.
  • Functions: set_principal(p), get_principal() -> RequestPrincipal | None and reset_principal().
  • A principal_context(p) context manager, which restores the previous value on exit.

  • require_admin_principal() -> RequestPrincipal. It raises PrincipalRequiredError(PermissionError) in each of these cases:

    • the principal is None,
    • the role is not core.security.ADMIN (rbac.py:25),
    • the email is blank after strip().

    It returns the principal with the stripped email. - src/core/security/__init__.py exports the new names.

docs.title: Auth layer
docs.text:
• require_auth() (src/ui/components/auth.py:251) calls set_principal(RequestPrincipal(user["email"], user["role"])) next to set_current_tenant.
  • _sign_out (auth.py:229) and logout_button (auth.py:286) call reset_principal() next to reset_current_tenant().

docs.title: Store
docs.text: PostgreSQLStore.reject(self, document_id: str) -> None: - The admin parameter is removed. - require_admin_principal() runs first, before any session opens. - The DELETE RETURNING and the audit INSERT stay in one transaction, with admin=principal.email.

docs.title: Migration
docs.text: A new revision with down_revision = "b7e2d41c9a30". Alembic runs it as lawbyai_owner. - upgrade: SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s', then REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE ON public.rejected_document FROM lawbyai_app. - downgrade: SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s', then GRANT UPDATE, DELETE ON public.rejected_document TO lawbyai_app. TRUNCATE is not granted, because b7e2d41c9a30:285 never granted it. - SELECT, INSERT and the sequence grants do not change. - The docstring states the retention rule: rows are kept forever, and only the owner can fix or purge a row.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• DBA fix F1. These cleanup fixtures run DELETE FROM rejected_document and must connect as the owner through get_settings().postgres_owner_url, as tests/integration/plugins/test_postgres.py:32-33 does for TRUNCATE. Where one transaction deletes from legal_document and rejected_document, move the whole block to the owner engine:
  • tests/integration/test_fetch_rejection.py:51
  • tests/integration/test_fetch_worker_pool.py:60-63
  • tests/integration/test_fetch_task_integration.py:68-71
  • tests/integration/test_reject_document.py:49
  • Reject calls. Change the 12 test calls reject(id, admin) to use principal_context. A new thread does not inherit context variables, so each _worker in the concurrency test (tests/integration/test_reject_document.py:178-181) enters principal_context itself.
  • DBA fix F2. The migration sets lock_timeout (see Migration).
  • Privileges, as lawbyai_app. Run each statement in its own transaction:
  • UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE each fail with 42501.
  • INSERT and SELECT succeed.
  • Schema guard (reads the schema after alembic upgrade head, not a fixed revision).
  • has_table_privilege returns false for UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE.
  • has_any_column_privilege(..., 'UPDATE') returns false (DBA fix F3).
  • PUBLIC has no rights on the table.
  • Migration, as the owner.
  • upgrade, downgrade and upgrade again.
  • After the downgrade, UPDATE and DELETE are true and TRUNCATE is still false (DBA fix F4).
  • reject().
  • These cases each raise and leave 0 audit rows and the document in place: no principal, a blank email, an email of spaces, and a role that is not admin.
  • The actor in the audit row equals the principal's email.
  • Auth.
  • require_auth() sets the principal.
  • Sign-out clears the principal.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• reject must run in the same Streamlit script run as require_auth(), after require_admin.
  • These are known limits:
  • A Celery task or other non-UI caller has no principal, so it cannot reject.
  • In-process code can still call set_principal. This is a trust boundary inside the process.
  • These items are out of scope and become follow-ups:
  • a reject UI page and its error display,
  • recording the retention rule in ADR-0016, which needs its own adr/ PR,
  • an actor for callers outside the UI.

docs.title: Business Goals
docs.text:
• An admin's reject decision is an audit record. Nobody can change or delete it through the app role lawbyai_app.
  • The actor in the record is the authenticated admin. A caller cannot write another person's email.
  • The retention rule is decided: rows are kept forever. Only the migration owner lawbyai_owner can fix or purge a row by hand. ADR-0016 records this rule.
  • Why now: the table exists (migration 963e40b83003) and b7e2d41c9a30 grants UPDATE and DELETE on it to the app role. The table is not yet used by a production caller, so the change is cheap now.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL with three roles from docker/initdb/00-roles.sh: lawbyai_owner (owns objects, runs Alembic), lawbyai_app (app and worker), lawbyai_auth (NOLOGIN).
  • The change is one new Alembic revision after head b7e2d41c9a30. It revokes UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on rejected_document from lawbyai_app. SELECT and INSERT stay. The sequence grants stay.
  • The owner keeps all rights (user decision: owner only, no trigger).
  • PostgreSQLStore.reject takes the actor from the request context, the same way the tenant guard reads core.security.tenant. It no longer takes a free admin argument.
  • The actor value comes from the authenticated session (get_current_user() in src/ui/components/auth.py) and is set in the context by the UI layer. The store does not import the UI.
  • No new dependency. Python 3.13, SQLAlchemy 2.x, Alembic.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• reject() runs with no actor in the context: it raises an error before any write. No document is deleted and no audit row is written.
  • The actor in the context is an empty or blank string: same as no actor.
  • Two concurrent rejects of one document: unchanged, only one deletes the row and writes the audit row.
  • The app role runs UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE on rejected_document: PostgreSQL denies it with SQLSTATE 42501.
  • The app role runs INSERT and SELECT: both still work.
  • The migration downgrade, run as the owner: it restores UPDATE and DELETE to the app role, as in b7e2d41c9a30, and TRUNCATE only if b7e2d41c9a30 granted it.

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• A later migration runs GRANT ALL ON ALL TABLES to the app role and silently restores UPDATE and DELETE. A test must catch this: it checks has_table_privilege for the app role on the head schema.
  • A caller sets the actor in the context and never clears it, so a later reject in the same thread uses a stale actor. The context helper must reset the value after the request (same pattern as the tenant context).
  • The reject fails because no actor is set: the UI shows an error, and the document stays.
  • What must survive: every existing audit row, the reject transaction (delete plus insert in one transaction), and the owner's ability to downgrade.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
• 3 of 3 denied statements: an integration test as lawbyai_app gets 42501 for UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on rejected_document.
  • 2 of 2 allowed statements: INSERT and SELECT as lawbyai_app succeed.
  • 1 test: reject() with no actor raises and writes 0 rows.
  • 1 test: the audit row's actor equals the actor in the context, not any caller argument.
  • Upgrade, downgrade and upgrade again pass as the owner in the Docker suite, with 0 failures.
  • Quality gate: ruff, ruff format --check, pyright and pytest pass. diff-cover is 90% or more on changed lines.

docs.title: Core idea
docs.text: A new core.security.actor module copies the pattern of tenant.py. It holds the email of the authenticated admin in its own ContextVar. reject(document_id) reads the actor and raises an error before any write when the actor is missing or blank. One migration revokes UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on rejected_document from lawbyai_app.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• src/core/security/actor.py (new): _ACTOR_VAR ("core.actor", default None) and these helpers:
  • set_current_actor(actor: str | None) -> None
  • get_current_actor() -> str | None
  • reset_current_actor() -> None
  • actor_context(actor): a context manager that restores the previous value in finally.
  • require_actor() -> str: returns the stripped actor. It raises MissingActorError when the actor is None or blank.
  • src/core/security/__init__.py: export the actor helpers, as it exports the tenant helpers.
  • src/ui/components/auth.py: wrap each admin reject action in actor_context(user.email). The email comes from get_current_user(). If no user is signed in, the actor is never set.
  • PostgreSQLStore.reject(self, document_id: str) -> None (src/plugins/relational_db/postgres.py:373):
  • Remove the admin parameter.
  • Call require_actor() first.
  • Keep the DELETE and INSERT transaction as it is, with admin=actor.
  • migrations/versions/<new>_revoke_rejected_document_mutation.py: down_revision = "b7e2d41c9a30".

docs.title: Migration SQL
docs.text:
b7e2d41c9a30 (lines 282-301) grants SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on rejected_document to the app role. It does not grant TRUNCATE. - upgrade: REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE ON public.rejected_document FROM lawbyai_app. TRUNCATE has no effect, because the app role never had it. The statement still makes the denial explicit. - downgrade: GRANT UPDATE, DELETE ON public.rejected_document TO lawbyai_app. This gives back the exact prior privileges, without TRUNCATE.

SELECT, INSERT and the sequence grants do not change. Alembic runs as lawbyai_owner, which owns the table.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
1. The UI handler calls get_current_user().
  2. The handler opens actor_context(email) and calls store.reject(doc_id).
  3. require_actor() runs. A missing or blank actor raises MissingActorError, and no transaction opens.
  4. The transaction runs DELETE RETURNING and then the INSERT of the audit row.
  5. After the commit, the delete hook runs.
  6. actor_context restores the previous actor.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Unit:
  • set, get and reset of the actor.
  • Nested actor_context restores the previous value.
  • The actor does not leak after an exception.
  • require_actor raises on None, "" and " ".
  • Store integration:
  • With no actor, reject raises, the document is still there, and no audit row is written.
  • The actor in the audit row is the actor from the context.
  • reject has no admin parameter.
  • Privilege integration (as lawbyai_app):
  • UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE each fail with 42501.
  • INSERT and SELECT succeed.
  • has_table_privilege returns false for UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE.
  • Migration:
  • upgrade, downgrade and upgrade again, as the owner.
  • After the downgrade, UPDATE and DELETE are granted again, and TRUNCATE is not.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text:
These cases are handled: - A missing or blank actor raises an error before any write. - finally clears a stale actor. - A later GRANT ALL is caught by the has_table_privilege test. - The downgrade is exact.

This case is not handled: - In-process code can call set_current_actor with a false email. This is a trust boundary, not a technical block.

docs.title: Effort and risks
docs.text:
Effort: S.

Risks: - The context variable must be set in the same call path as reject. Streamlit reruns and OS threads do not carry it. - The signature of reject changes, so the tests that pass admin must change too.

docs.title: Core idea
docs.text: One frozen RequestPrincipal(tenant_id, email, role) holds the identity of the request. require_auth() sets it once in each request. reject() reads the principal. It requires the role admin and an email that is not blank. A new migration revokes UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on rejected_document from lawbyai_app.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• src/core/security/principal.py (new):
  • @dataclass(frozen=True) RequestPrincipal(tenant_id: str, email: str, role: str).
  • Functions: set_principal(p), get_principal() -> RequestPrincipal | None and reset_principal().
  • principal_context(p): restores the previous principal on exit.
  • PrincipalRequiredError(PermissionError).
  • src/core/security/__init__.py: exports the new names. tenant.py does not change.
  • src/ui/components/auth.py:251: after set_current_tenant, call set_principal(RequestPrincipal(...)). The values come from the user dict that require_auth() reads from the DB.
  • auth.py, _sign_out and logout_button: call reset_principal() next to reset_current_tenant().
  • postgres.py:373:
  • The signature becomes reject(self, document_id: str) -> None.
  • A guard runs before any session opens.
  • The guard raises PrincipalRequiredError if the principal is None, if role != "admin", or if the email is blank.
  • A new migration with down_revision = "b7e2d41c9a30".

docs.title: Migration SQL
docs.text:
• upgrade: REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE ON public.rejected_document FROM lawbyai_app.
  • downgrade: GRANT UPDATE, DELETE ON public.rejected_document TO lawbyai_app.

The downgrade gives back the exact prior privileges. b7e2d41c9a30:285 grants only SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, so the downgrade does not grant TRUNCATE.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
1. require_auth() sets the tenant and the principal on each rerun.
  2. The admin rejects a document.
  3. store.reject(id) validates the principal before it touches the DB.
  4. One transaction runs DELETE RETURNING and then inserts the audit row with admin=principal.email.
  5. On sign-out, the principal is reset.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• As lawbyai_app:
  • UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE each fail with 42501.
  • INSERT and SELECT succeed.
  • has_table_privilege returns false for UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE.
  • Migration, as the owner:
  • upgrade, downgrade and upgrade again.
  • After the downgrade, UPDATE and DELETE are granted again, and TRUNCATE is not.
  • reject():
  • Each of these cases raises, writes 0 audit rows and keeps the document: no principal, a blank email, an email of spaces, and a role that is not admin.
  • The actor in the audit row is the principal's email.
  • reject(id, admin="x") raises TypeError.
  • Auth:
  • require_auth() sets the principal.
  • Sign-out clears the principal.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text:
These cases are handled: - A missing or blank actor raises an error before any write. - A role that is not admin raises an error before any write. - A stale principal is cleared by the reset and by the restore in principal_context. - A later GRANT ALL is caught by the has_table_privilege test.

This case is not handled: - In-process code can call set_principal with false values. This is a trust boundary.

docs.title: Effort and risks
docs.text:
Effort: M. The change touches the auth layer, the store, a new security module, a migration and the Docker-suite tests.

Risks: - Streamlit threading: the principal must be set in the same script run as the reject call. - The role string and the keys of the user dict are assumptions. Check them against _public() first. - The tenant and the principal hold the same tenant id, so the two values can drift apart.

docs.title: T1: Add RequestPrincipal module and exports
Context
docs.text: The reject audit needs a trusted actor from the request, not a free argument. This task adds the principal context that the auth layer sets and the store reads. It serves the requirement that a caller cannot write another person's email, and the stale-actor failure mode.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text: Create src/core/security/principal.py, modelled on src/core/security/tenant.py:37-85 (a ContextVar with set, get, reset and a restoring context manager). - @dataclass(frozen=True) RequestPrincipal(email: str, role: str). No tenant_id. - set_principal(p), get_principal() -> RequestPrincipal | None, reset_principal(). - principal_context(p) context manager: restores the previous value in finally. - PrincipalRequiredError(PermissionError). - require_admin_principal() -> RequestPrincipal: raise PrincipalRequiredError when the principal is None, the role is not ADMIN (src/core/security/rbac.py:25), or email.strip() is empty. Return a principal with the stripped email. - Export the new names in src/core/security/__init__.py (imports at lines 22-41, __all__ at 43-61) and add a "Principal" block to the module docstring. - Import ADMIN from .rbac, not from the package, to avoid a cycle. - Tests go in tests/unit/core/security/test_principal.py.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
Scenario: set, get and reset
  Given no principal is set
  When set_principal is called with an admin principal and then reset_principal is called
  Then get_principal returns the principal after set and None after reset

Scenario: context manager restores the previous value
  Given principal A is set
  When code runs inside principal_context(B) and raises an exception
  Then get_principal returns B inside the block and A after it

Scenario: missing principal is refused
  Given no principal is set
  When require_admin_principal is called
  Then it raises PrincipalRequiredError

Scenario: non-admin is refused
  Given a principal with role "user"
  When require_admin_principal is called
  Then it raises PrincipalRequiredError

Scenario: blank email is refused
  Given an admin principal with email "   "
  When require_admin_principal is called
  Then it raises PrincipalRequiredError

Scenario: admin passes with a stripped email
  Given an admin principal with email " a@x.pl "
  When require_admin_principal is called
  Then it returns a principal whose email is "a@x.pl"

docs.text:

  • Tests exist for every scenario and pass.
  • The quality gate reports pass or skipped (never fail).
  • No OPEN: item remains.

docs.title: T2: Alembic revision to make rejected_document append-only for the app role
Context
docs.text: Today lawbyai_app can UPDATE and DELETE rows in rejected_document (granted by b7e2d41c9a30). The audit log must be immutable for the app role. This task adds the revision that removes those rights. It serves the business goal that only the owner can change or purge a row.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text: Add one file in migrations/versions/ with down_revision = "b7e2d41c9a30". Alembic runs it as lawbyai_owner. Context

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text: Create tests/integration/test_rejected_document_privileges.py, marked integration, skipped when PostgreSQL is unreachable (as tests/integration/test_reject_document.py:1-22 does, with can_connect). - App engine: get_settings().postgres_url. After the downgrade UPDATE and DELETE are true and TRUNCATE is false. Always restore head in a finally. - Resolved: reuse the Alembic command.upgrade / command.downgrade pattern of tests/integration/test_rls_hardening.py and tests/integration/test_document_status_migration.py, run with the owner URL.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The app, the worker, the tests and Alembic all connect as one role (POSTGRES_USER). That role is the bootstrap superuser and the table owner, so it bypasses RLS. The policies on users and tenants also allow every row when app.current_tenant = ''. The login lookup must read one user across tenants before any tenant is known.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Path 1, privileged database function: one NOBYPASSRLS app role. A SECURITY DEFINER auth_lookup_user is the only cross-tenant read. Effort M.
  • Path 2, split connections: a second engine connects as a BYPASSRLS login role for the lookup. Effort M.
  • Path 3, policy-only: an extra SELECT policy keyed on app.login_email. Effort S to M.
  • Path 4, schema split: a global auth.credentials table, separate from users. Effort L.
Path 1 Path 2 Path 3 Path 4 Fit to constraints all items no function, LOGIN auth role no function, no auth role all items, plus a model split Handles failure modes yes yes yes yes Complexity moderate two engines, two secrets low high Effort M M S-M L Main risk function grants or search_path app holds a BYPASSRLS login forged setting reads a hash write paths drift

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: The user chose Path 1. Reasons: - It meets every requirement and every metric, including the pg_proc checks. - The cross-tenant login path returns at most one row with fixed columns, by exact email. RLS stops app queries that leave out the tenant. RLS does not stop SQL injection, because injected SQL can set app.current_tenant itself. Parameterized SQL is still the defence against injection. - It adds no runtime component and does not move data.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: These items include the fixes from the dba review and the solution-architect review.

docs.title: Roles (init script docker/initdb/00-roles.sh, fresh volumes only)
docs.text:
• lawbyai_owner: LOGIN, NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS. It gets CREATE, USAGE ON SCHEMA public (PG15+ needs this). It runs migrations and owns every object.
  • lawbyai_app: LOGIN, NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS, NOINHERIT, NOCREATEDB, NOCREATEROLE. It owns nothing.
  • lawbyai_auth: NOLOGIN, BYPASSRLS, NOINHERIT, NOCREATEDB, NOCREATEROLE. It gets CREATE and USAGE on public (ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER needs CREATE for the new owner) and column SELECT on users (id, tenant_id, email, role, name, is_active, password_hash, session_version) only.
  • GRANT lawbyai_auth TO lawbyai_owner WITH INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE, so the owner can set the function owner. Recorded risk: the owner can SET ROLE to a BYPASSRLS role and create objects that this role owns. The app cannot. A test checks that lawbyai_auth owns only auth_lookup_user.
  • Passwords come from env. Compose passes them to postgres.

docs.title: Connections and migrations
docs.text:
• Settings get a separate owner URL for migrations. migrations/env.py and the init service use it.
  • PostgreSQLStore.initialize() no longer runs Alembic upgrade. It only checks that the DB is at head, and fails clearly if not. lawbyai_app gets SELECT on alembic_version.
  • The app, the worker and the tests connect as lawbyai_app.
  • The init service runs alembic upgrade head with the owner URL. It then runs the bootstrap store with the app URL, so get_login_user has EXECUTE.
  • The test service runs alembic upgrade head with the owner URL before pytest, because initialize() no longer migrates.

docs.title: Migration (new revision, down_revision = "77985ac8fa22", SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s')
docs.text:
1. Check that the three roles exist, and that lawbyai_owner owns tenants, users, legal_document, rejected_document and alembic_version. If not, stop and name what is missing.
  2. A migration that reads data runs ALTER TABLE ... NO FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and then FORCE again in the same transaction (user decision). A test asserts that FORCE is on at head.
  3. users.tenant_id is already NOT NULL (since 4439761c5e40), so this revision does not change it. Every row read of this revision runs inside the NO FORCE window of step 2. ALTER TABLE ... NO FORCE/FORCE takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE under the 5s lock_timeout. Step 1 also checks the owner of the function users_bump_session_version.
  4. ALTER POLICY (names kept) to tenant_id = nullif(current_setting('app.current_tenant', true), '') (id on tenants), for USING and WITH CHECK. No tenant means zero rows.
  5. Create public.auth_lookup_user(p_email text) RETURNS TABLE (id, tenant_id, email, role, name, is_active, password_hash, session_version): LANGUAGE sql, STABLE, STRICT, SECURITY DEFINER, SET search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp. The body reads public.users WHERE email = lower(btrim(p_email)). Run ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO lawbyai_auth, REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC and GRANT EXECUTE ... TO lawbyai_app.
  6. Grants for lawbyai_app: DML on tenants, users, legal_document and rejected_document, USAGE and SELECT on the rejected_document id sequence, and SELECT on alembic_version. ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE lawbyai_owner REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM PUBLIC. Each later migration grants per table.
  7. The downgrade drops the function, revokes the grants, restores the old policies with ALTER POLICY exactly as 4439761c5e40 defines them, and undoes the ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES revoke. It keeps ck_users_email_normalised, which belongs to 77985ac8fa22.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• get_login_user calls auth_lookup_user and keeps its signature and its dict keys. without_tenant() is no longer needed there.
  • The bootstrap (src/bootstrap/init_stack.py) runs ensure_tenant and the admin step inside the tenant context of INIT_TENANT_ID. It finds the admin through get_login_user.
  • list_tenants has only the bootstrap as a caller, and it now returns the current tenant only.
  • get_user_by_email stays tenant-scoped. Its docstring says that it returns None with no tenant set.
  • Update the module docstring and the TENANT_SETTING comment in postgres.py.

docs.title: Old volumes
docs.text: The docs give the SQL to create the roles and to run per-object ALTER ... OWNER TO lawbyai_owner for the tables, the rejected_document sequence and the function users_bump_session_version. The docs SQL also mirrors the init script: CREATE, USAGE ON SCHEMA public for the owner and GRANT lawbyai_auth TO lawbyai_owner WITH INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE. REASSIGN OWNED cannot be used, because the old role is the bootstrap superuser.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Fixtures create and truncate data as the owner inside a tenant context, and assert as lawbyai_app.
  • The test service depends on the init script roles. CI starts from a fresh volume.
  • Fix the tests that use users with no tenant: test_users_login_store.py, test_login_flow.py and test_init_stack.py.
  • Extra metrics: proowner = lawbyai_auth, has_function_privilege('public', ..., 'EXECUTE') = false, the app cannot SET ROLE lawbyai_auth, and FORCE RLS is on at head.

docs.title: Accepted trade-offs
docs.text:
• We give up the smaller effort of Path 3 and the full data split of Path 4.
  • Residual leak: uq_users_email is global, so create_user shows whether an email exists in another tenant.

docs.title: Business Goals
docs.text:
• A bug in app code cannot read or write the users or tenants rows of another tenant.
  • Login still works for every tenant, before any tenant is known.
  • Why now: the login UI is merged, and the dba found that the RLS on users protects nothing.
  • Out of scope: RLS on legal_document (a later issue). No change to the login UI.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, Docker Compose. Runs on 4-6 GB RAM.
  • Three roles: lawbyai_owner (runs migrations, owns tables), lawbyai_app (LOGIN, NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS, owns nothing), lawbyai_auth (NOLOGIN, BYPASSRLS, column SELECT on users only).
  • A Postgres init script in docker-entrypoint-initdb.d creates the roles. Passwords come from env.
  • public.auth_lookup_user(p_email text): LANGUAGE sql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, SET search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp, owner lawbyai_auth. EXECUTE only for lawbyai_app.
  • PostgreSQLStore.get_login_user keeps its signature and calls the function.
  • The migration keeps lock_timeout. The downgrade restores the old policies and drops the function. It keeps ck_users_email_normalised, which belongs to revision 77985ac8fa22.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• Email ' A@x.PL ' matches the stored a@x.pl (lower and trim).
  • Email '%', '' or an unknown email returns zero rows. No pattern match.
  • A user with is_active = false is returned. The UI keeps its own reject.
  • Mixed-case or duplicate emails: revision 77985ac8fa22 already adds ck_users_email_normalised with a pre-check. This issue keeps that CHECK.
  • No tenant set during bootstrap or migrations: both still see all rows they need (see decision.md).

docs.title: Failure Modes
docs.text:
• Old volume without the new roles: the migration stops and names the missing roles. Docs give the SQL to create them.
  • No tenant set: SELECT count(*) FROM users returns 0 (fail closed).
  • Tenant A set: an INSERT of a tenant B row fails the WITH CHECK.
  • The app never connects as a superuser or table owner.

docs.title: Success Metrics
docs.text:
• 0 rows visible in users and tenants with no tenant set, as lawbyai_app.
  • auth_lookup_user(' A@x.PL ') returns exactly 1 row across 2 tenants with no tenant set.
  • rolsuper = false and rolbypassrls = false for current_user in 100% of app and test connections.
  • pg_proc.prosecdef = true, search_path set in proconfig, and 0 EXECUTE grants to PUBLIC.
  • All Docker integration tests pass as lawbyai_app. diff-cover is 90% or more.

docs.title: Path 1: privileged database function
docs.text: The app has one login role with no bypass. A SECURITY DEFINER function, owned by a NOLOGIN BYPASSRLS role, is the only cross-tenant read path.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• docker/initdb/00-roles.sh is mounted into docker-entrypoint-initdb.d. It creates three roles, with passwords from env.
  • A new Alembic revision after 4439761c5e40.
  • public.auth_lookup_user(p_email text): LANGUAGE sql, STABLE, SECURITY DEFINER, SET search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp, owner lawbyai_auth.
  • Compose and settings: the app, worker and test services use lawbyai_app. Migrations use lawbyai_owner.

docs.title: Roles and grants
docs.text:
• lawbyai_owner owns the tables and runs migrations.
  • lawbyai_app is LOGIN, NOSUPERUSER and NOBYPASSRLS. It gets DML on the tables and EXECUTE on the function.
  • lawbyai_auth is NOLOGIN and BYPASSRLS. It gets column SELECT on users only.
  • The function has no EXECUTE for PUBLIC. Default privileges keep new tables private.

docs.title: Migration
docs.text:
1. Set lock_timeout. Check that the roles exist. Check the emails for mixed case and for duplicates.
  2. Keep the existing email CHECK ck_users_email_normalised (revision 77985ac8fa22).
  3. Replace the policies with tenant_id = nullif(current_setting('app.current_tenant', true), '') (id on tenants), for USING and for WITH CHECK.
  4. Create the function and the grants. The downgrade restores the old policies and drops the function. It keeps the email CHECK.

docs.title: Code change
docs.text: get_login_user runs SELECT * FROM auth_lookup_user(:e). The signature stays the same, and without_tenant() is no longer needed.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text: All listed failure modes are handled. Open: the bootstrap must create the first tenant and admin with no tenant set.

docs.title: Assessment
docs.text:
• Complexity: moderate.
  • Effort: M.
  • Main risk: the function is the single point of trust. A wrong search_path or grant reopens cross-tenant reads. The pg_proc metrics cover this.

docs.title: Path 2: split connections
docs.text: The app holds two engines. A tenant engine connects as lawbyai_app (NOBYPASSRLS). A small auth engine connects as lawbyai_auth (LOGIN, BYPASSRLS) and only the login lookup uses it.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• The tenant engine keeps the begin hook. The auth engine has no hook and a pool of 1 to 2 connections.
  • An init script creates three roles. Compose and settings get a second DSN and a second password.

docs.title: Roles and grants
docs.text:
• lawbyai_app gets DML on the tables.
  • lawbyai_auth gets column SELECT on users only.
  • lawbyai_owner runs migrations.

docs.title: Migration
docs.text: The roles check, the email check, the CHECK and the fail-closed policies are the same as in path 1. There is no function.

docs.title: Code change
docs.text:
• get_login_user selects explicit columns through the auth engine.
  • A startup assertion checks the attributes of both roles.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text: All listed failure modes are handled. It deviates from the requirements: lawbyai_auth is LOGIN, and the pg_proc metrics do not apply.

docs.title: Assessment
docs.text:
• Complexity: two engines, two pools and two secrets.
  • Effort: M.
  • Main risk: the app process holds a BYPASSRLS login that can read every password_hash. An SQL injection is not limited to one row.

docs.title: Path 3: policy-only
docs.text: Path 3 has one NOBYPASSRLS app role, and RLS policies alone allow the login read. It has no function and no lawbyai_auth.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• Roles: lawbyai_owner and lawbyai_app.
  • Policies on users and tenants (fail closed): tenant_id = nullif(current_setting('app.current_tenant', true), '').
  • Policy users_login is FOR SELECT only. Its condition is that email equals lower(btrim(current_setting('app.login_email', true))) and that the setting is not empty.
  • CHECK (email = lower(btrim(email))) plus the unique email gives at most one row.

docs.title: Migration
docs.text: Check the roles and the emails. Add the CHECK. Replace the policies, and apply the grants. The downgrade restores the old policies.

docs.title: Code change
docs.text: get_login_user sets app.login_email (transaction-local) and then runs the same select.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text: All listed failure modes are handled. It deviates from the requirements: it has no function and no lawbyai_auth.

docs.title: Assessment
docs.text:
• Complexity: low.
  • Effort: S to M.
  • Main risk: any code on the app connection can set app.login_email and read one known user's full row, with password_hash, in any tenant. A policy cannot hide columns.

docs.title: Path 4: schema split
docs.text: Login data moves to a global auth.credentials table. It has strict grants and no tenant RLS. users keeps only tenant data under fail-closed RLS.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
• auth.credentials(user_id PK/FK, email UNIQUE CHECK(email = lower(btrim(email))), password_hash, role, tenant_id, is_active, session_version).
  • public.users(id, tenant_id, name) and public.tenants keep RLS. Policy: tenant_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.current_tenant', true), '').
  • auth_lookup_user(p_email) (SECURITY DEFINER) is the only read path into auth.

docs.title: Roles and grants
docs.text:
• lawbyai_owner owns the schema and the tables, and runs migrations.
  • lawbyai_app is LOGIN, NOSUPERUSER and NOBYPASSRLS. It has no USAGE on auth, and EXECUTE on the function only.
  • lawbyai_auth is NOLOGIN. It has SELECT on auth.credentials, and it does not need BYPASSRLS.
  • The function has no EXECUTE for PUBLIC. ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES keeps new tables private. An init script creates the roles.

docs.title: Migration
docs.text:
1. Check that the roles exist. Check the emails for mixed case and for duplicates.
  2. Create the schema and the table, and backfill them from users.
  3. Drop the credential columns from users. Replace the policies.
  4. Create the function and the grants. The downgrade copies the columns back.

docs.title: Code change
docs.text:
• get_login_user calls the function.
  • create_user, bump_session_version and the bootstrap need more definer functions for writes.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text: All listed failure modes are handled. The definer write functions bypass tenant checks by design.

docs.title: Assessment
docs.text:
• Complexity: high. This is a data move plus a model split.
  • Effort: L.
  • Main risk: the write paths of users and credentials drift apart, and old code that expects users.email breaks.

docs.title: T1 Init script for three roles
Context
docs.text: Today one role is superuser and table owner, so RLS protects nothing. This task creates the three roles of the design on fresh volumes. It serves the Technical Constraints on roles and the success metric rolsuper = false and rolbypassrls = false.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
• Create docker/initdb/00-roles.sh. The postgres image runs it once on an empty volume, as the bootstrap superuser (POSTGRES_USER).
  • Use psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1. psql reads the passwords from env with \getenv, so they never appear in the file or in the process list.
  • Role names are fixed: lawbyai_owner, lawbyai_app, lawbyai_auth.
  • lawbyai_owner: LOGIN, NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS, no CREATEDB. GRANT CREATE, USAGE ON SCHEMA public. Database ownership is not required.
  • lawbyai_app: LOGIN, NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS, NOINHERIT, NOCREATEDB, NOCREATEROLE.
  • lawbyai_auth: NOLOGIN, BYPASSRLS, NOINHERIT, NOCREATEDB, NOCREATEROLE. GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public.
  • The init script only creates roles, memberships and schema grants. It does not grant column SELECT on users, because the table does not exist at init time. T4 grants it in the migration.
  • GRANT lawbyai_auth TO lawbyai_owner WITH INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE.
  • Env variables: POSTGRES_USER and POSTGRES_PASSWORD stay the bootstrap superuser. Only the postgres service and the init script use them. Two new variables hold the login passwords: LAWBYAI_OWNER_PASSWORD and LAWBYAI_APP_PASSWORD.
  • docker/docker-compose.yml, service postgres (line 59 environment:): pass the two new passwords and mount ./initdb:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro. The service is read_only: true with user: "70:70", so the script must be readable by uid 70 and executable or run through sh.
  • docker/.env.example: add the two passwords with change-me values (the init program rejects change-me prefixes for secrets in validate_config).

docs.title: T3 Migration part 1: role checks, NO FORCE window, tenant-only policies
Context
docs.text: The policies on users and tenants show every row when app.current_tenant = '', so a missing tenant leaks all data. This revision checks the roles, then closes that gap so no tenant means zero rows. It serves the metrics "0 rows with no tenant set" and "tenant A cannot write tenant B".

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
• New file in migrations/versions/, down_revision = "77985ac8fa22". T4 adds its steps to the same revision file. The two tasks share one revision, so T4 starts after T3 is merged.
  • First statement: SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'.
  • Step 1, checks: query pg_roles for the three roles. Query pg_class and pg_proc owners for tenants, users, legal_document, rejected_document, alembic_version and the function users_bump_session_version. Raise RuntimeError naming each missing role or wrong owner. The four-table list in decision.md is the ownership check only.
  • Step 2, NO FORCE window: ALTER TABLE ... NO FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on tenants and users, do every data read of this revision, then ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on the same two tables in the same transaction.
  • Step 4: ALTER POLICY with the existing names (read them from 4439761c5e40) to tenant_id = nullif(current_setting('app.current_tenant', true), '') for USING and WITH CHECK. On tenants use id.
  • FORCE stays as migration 4439761c5e40 set it (lines 58 and 69): on tenants and users only. legal_document and rejected_document get no RLS and no FORCE. Do not change that.
  • The downgrade is in T4.

docs.title: T4 Migration part 2: auth_lookup_user, grants, downgrade
Context
docs.text: Login must read one user across tenants before a tenant is known. After T3 the policies block that read. This task adds the only cross-tenant read, a SECURITY DEFINER function, and the grants for the app role. It serves the metrics on pg_proc and PUBLIC EXECUTE.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
• Same revision file as T3, in migrations/versions/.
  • Step 5: CREATE FUNCTION public.auth_lookup_user(p_email text) RETURNS TABLE (id varchar, tenant_id varchar, email varchar, role varchar, name varchar, is_active boolean, password_hash varchar, session_version integer). Use LANGUAGE sql, STABLE, STRICT, SECURITY DEFINER, SET search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp. Body: SELECT ... FROM public.users u WHERE u.email = lower(btrim(p_email)). Column types must match User in src/plugins/relational_db/postgres.py (lines 74-86). Then REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC and GRANT EXECUTE ... TO lawbyai_app, and only after that ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO lawbyai_auth (the ACL moves with the owner). The downgrade drops the function under SET LOCAL ROLE lawbyai_auth, then RESET ROLE.
  • This migration grants lawbyai_auth column SELECT on users (id, tenant_id, email, role, name, is_active, password_hash, session_version). The init script does not grant it (T1).
  • Step 6: GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on tenants, users, legal_document, rejected_document to lawbyai_app. GRANT USAGE, SELECT on the rejected_document id sequence. GRANT SELECT ON alembic_version. ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE lawbyai_owner REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM PUBLIC.
  • Step 7, downgrade(): drop the function, revoke the grants (including the lawbyai_auth column SELECT), restore the old policies with ALTER POLICY exactly as 4439761c5e40 defines them, undo the default privileges revoke. Keep ck_users_email_normalised. FORCE: 4439761c5e40 sets FORCE only on tenants and users. The downgrade leaves FORCE on those two tables as it was, and sets none on legal_document or rejected_document.
  • The existing test test_downgrade_removes_objects_and_keeps_lowercase_emails uses PREVIOUS_REVISION = "963e40b83003" and must still pass.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Each success metric and edge case in requirements.md needs a test that fails when the control breaks. This task adds one test file that covers them against a live PostgreSQL as lawbyai_app. It serves every success metric and every edge case.

docs.title: Technical Approach
docs.text:
• Create tests/integration/test_rls_hardening.py. Mark it pytest.mark.integration. Use postgres_url (app) and owner_url from tests/integration/conftest.py (T7).
  • Setup: as the owner, in a tenant context (app.current_tenant set in each transaction), insert one user in tenant A with email a@x.pl, one in tenant B, and one inactive user. Use unique emails and tenant ids per test run. Delete them afterwards, per tenant.

  • Metric queries: pg_roles for current_user; pg_proc for prosecdef, proconfig, proowner::regrole; has_function_privilege('public', 'public.auth_lookup_user(text)', 'EXECUTE'); pg_class.relforcerowsecurity.
  • Edge cases: auth_lookup_user(' A@x.PL '), '%', '', unknown email, inactive user.
  • Cross-tenant write: set app.current_tenant to A and INSERT a tenant B user. Expect psycopg InsufficientPrivilege or DBAPIError with the RLS message.
  • SET ROLE lawbyai_auth as the app: expect an error.
  • FORCE: tenants and users have FORCE on. legal_document and rejected_document have no FORCE and no RLS.
